title: Szepesvari-2010-AlgorithmsForReinforcementLearning
gse_mapping: The GSE play-call engine is an MDP: state x = (down, distance, field position, formation, personnel, score, time), action a = the play/coverage call, transition kernel P0 = the stochastic outcome of that call. The 10,000-world crucible simulator IS an empirical estimate of P0. The Markov property is the modeling assumption that the current game state summarizes all relevant history.
verbatim_quote: Markov Decision Processes are a tool for modeling sequential decision-making problems where a decision maker interacts with a system in a sequential fashion.

title: Szepesvari-2010-AlgorithmsForReinforcementLearning
primitive_name: Discounted return and the optimal behavior objective
gse_mapping: GSE's objective is the discounted expected return of a drive/game: immediate yards/EPA plus gamma-discounted future win-probability. The discount factor gamma is GSE's tempo dial — how much a play's future consequences (field position, down-distance) weigh against its immediate gain. The crucible maximizes expected return over the play-call policy, from every game state.
verbatim_quote: The goal of the decision-maker is to choose a behavior that maximizes the expected return, irrespectively of how the process is started.

title: Szepesvari-2010-AlgorithmsForReinforcementLearning
gse_mapping: GSE's state-value V*(x) is the win-probability / expected points from a game state under optimal play-calling. The crucible computes V* by simulation, then the engine acts greedily w.r.t. it. This is the formal object the 10,000-world ensemble estimates: the value of every (down,distance,field-position) situation.
verbatim_quote: A behavior that achieves the optimal values in all states is optimal.

title: Szepesvari-2010-AlgorithmsForReinforcementLearning
primitive_name: Existence of an optimal stationary policy
gse_mapping: GSE need not search history-dependent play-call strategies: an optimal stationary policy (a mapping from game state to play call) exists and suffices. Derived kernel: GSE's policy search can be restricted to state->action maps (the playbook conditioned on situation), dramatically shrinking the search space, because no history-dependent scheme beats the best stationary one.
verbatim_quote: In the class of MDPs considered here, an optimal stationary policy always exists

title: Szepesvari-2010-AlgorithmsForReinforcementLearning
primitive_name: Bellman equations, contraction, and dynamic programming
gse_mapping: The Bellman equation IS the GSE crucible's recursive evaluation rule: the value of a game state equals the immediate reward plus the discounted value of the resulting state, maximized over play calls. The contraction property guarantees the crucible's backward induction converges to a unique value surface. The RLVR reward verifier checks the Bellman residual T*Q−Q as a consistency gate.
verbatim_quote: The above facts provide the basis for the value- and policy-iteration algorithms.

title: Szepesvari-2010-AlgorithmsForReinforcementLearning
gse_mapping: GSE's crucible runs value iteration (backward induction over the game tree) to estimate V*, then extracts a greedy play-call policy. The Singh-Yee bound quantifies how value-estimation error translates into play-call suboptimality: a Q-error of eps costs at most 2eps/(1−gamma) in value. Policy iteration is GSE's alternate refine-the-playbook loop (evaluate the current playbook, then improve it greedily).
verbatim_quote: After k iterations, policy iteration gives a policy not worse than the policy that is greedy w.r.t. to the value function computed using k iterations of value iteration if the two procedures are started with the same initial value function.

title: Szepesvari-2010-AlgorithmsForReinforcementLearning
gse_mapping: The TD error is GSE's calibration surprise signal: delta = realized EPA + gamma·(predicted value of the resulting state) − (predicted value of the current state). GSE updates its state-value estimates snap-by-snap using bootstrapping, without waiting for the drive to end — exactly how the engine learns online from partial drives. The crucible's per-snap value update is TD(0).
verbatim_quote: The unique feature of TD learning is that it uses bootstrapping: predictions are used as targets during the course of learning.

title: Szepesvari-2010-AlgorithmsForReinforcementLearning
gse_mapping: GSE's value-learning convergence rests on the same SA/ODE argument: the per-snap updates track a stable linear ODE whose fixed point is the true state value. Derived kernel: GSE verifies its value-learner's stability by checking the ODE eigenvalue condition (gamma P−I in the left half-plane) and the infinite-visitation requirement, rather than assuming convergence.
verbatim_quote: Just like many other algorithms in reinforcement learning, tabular TD(0) is a stochastic approximation (SA) algorithm.

title: Szepesvari-2010-AlgorithmsForReinforcementLearning
primitive_name: Robbins-Monro step sizes and the constant-step-size practice
gse_mapping: GSE's value-learner step size is a stationarity dial: decaying alpha_t for a stable calibration target, constant alpha for a shifting defense (non-stationary). The book's warning that constant step-sizes give convergence in distribution (persistent variance) is GSE's calibration-jitter floor — the engine must size alpha to the defense's adaptivity, and never claim point convergence while tracking a moving target.
verbatim_quote: In fact, in practice people often use constant step-sizes, which clearly violates the RM conditions.

title: Szepesvari-2010-AlgorithmsForReinforcementLearning
gse_mapping: TD(lambda) is GSE's drive-level credit assignment: a touchdown's reward must be credited back across the whole drive's plays, and lambda controls how far back the credit flows. Eligibility traces are GSE's mechanism for assigning a drive's outcome to the earlier play calls that enabled it. lambda=0 credits only the last snap; lambda=1 credits the whole drive (Monte-Carlo). GSE tunes lambda to the drive structure.
verbatim_quote: The previous examples show that both Monte-Carlo and TD(0) have their own merits.

title: Szepesvari-2010-AlgorithmsForReinforcementLearning
primitive_name: Function approximation for large state spaces
gse_mapping: GSE's game-state space is enormous (down×distance×field×formation×personnel×score×time), so its value function MUST be approximated: V_theta(x)=theta^T phi(x), where phi is the football ontology's feature map. Averager-style features (soft coverage-shell memberships summing to 1) keep the value learner max-norm well-behaved. The ontology features are the inductive bias that makes the huge state space learnable.
verbatim_quote: When the state space is large (or infinite), it is not feasible to keep a separate value for each state in the memory.

title: Szepesvari-2010-AlgorithmsForReinforcementLearning
primitive_name: Q-learning: off-policy learning from arbitrary sampling
gse_mapping: Q-learning is GSE's play-value learner: it learns the OPTIMAL play-call value Q* from the plays actually called (the behavior policy), not just from greedy plays. The max_a' backup means GSE learns what the best call WOULD have been even when a different call was made — the counterfactual the bandit layer said was unobservable is recovered here via the Bellman max. The infinite-visitation condition is GSE's exploration requirement.
verbatim_quote: A major attraction of Q-learning is its simplicity and that it allows one to use an arbitrary sampling strategy to generate the training data provided that in the limit, all state-action pairs are updated infinitely often.

title: Szepesvari-2010-AlgorithmsForReinforcementLearning
primitive_name: Q-learning's key insight: action-values are expectations
gse_mapping: GSE learns action-values Q*(state, play-call), not state-values, precisely because Q* is an expectation that can be estimated snap-by-snap from sampled outcomes. Derived kernel: GSE's model-free play-value learner targets Q* (the expectation form), and the crucible's value-iteration targets V* (the sup form) — the two are connected by V*(x)=max_a Q*(x,a), and GSE must not confuse which object admits incremental learning.
verbatim_quote: The key observation that lead to the discovery of Q-learning is that unlike the optimal state values, the optimal action-values can be expressed as expectations

title: Szepesvari-2010-AlgorithmsForReinforcementLearning
gse_mapping: GSE learns the optimal playbook OFF-POLICY from the historical record of plays actually called — it does not need to have called the optimal plays to learn their value. This is why GSE can mine decades of game film: the max backup recovers the best-call value from any called play. The off-policy nature is what makes the historical corpus usable, and the non-telescoping is why GSE's drive-credit assignment must cut traces on non-greedy calls.
verbatim_quote: Q-learning is an inherently off-policy algorithm: the temporal differences underlying Q-learning do not telescope even when

title: Szepesvari-2010-AlgorithmsForReinforcementLearning
gse_mapping: GSE's post-decision state is the resulting down-distance-field-position AFTER a play's deterministic effect but BEFORE the next stochastic event (e.g. the new line of scrimmage before the next play's outcome). Derived kernel: GSE learns the afterstate value V_A to avoid re-simulating the expectation at every action-selection step — the crucible computes greedy play calls as argmax_a r+gamma V_A(f(x,a)) without a nested stochastic optimization, a major compute saving.
verbatim_quote: Thus, the expectation is avoided, i.e., no stochastic optimization problem needs to be solved.

title: Szepesvari-2010-AlgorithmsForReinforcementLearning
primitive_name: Pure greed fails: exploration is mandatory
gse_mapping: GSE must explore non-greedy play calls: a engine that only ever calls its best-estimated play never learns whether a different call is better, and can lock onto a suboptimal playbook. This is the formal reason GSE's crucible probes alternative calls (the 10,000 worlds explore the action space) rather than only simulating the greedy line. Pure greed is the tout's 'lock' — provably fragile.
verbatim_quote: A basic observation then is that a bandit learner who always chooses the action with the best estimated payoff (i.e., who always makes the greedy choice) can fail to find the best action with positive probability, which in turn leads to a large loss.

title: Szepesvari-2010-AlgorithmsForReinforcementLearning
primitive_name: Optimism in the face of uncertainty (UCB1)
gse_mapping: GSE's play-call exploration uses OFU: it favors calls whose value is uncertain (few simulated reps), not just calls with the best mean estimate. The UCB bonus R√(2 log t/n_t) is GSE's uncertainty-driven exploration schedule — a play call tried in only a few crucible worlds gets an optimism bonus, ensuring the engine probes the whole playbook. This is the principled alternative to epsilon-greedy's blind randomness.
verbatim_quote: Notice that an action's UCB is larger if less information is available for it.

title: Szepesvari-2010-AlgorithmsForReinforcementLearning
gse_mapping: GSE's play-calling balances exploration (probing uncertain calls) and exploitation (calling the best-known play) via a softmax/Boltzmann policy over Q-values — the SAME entropic link function as the online layer's mirror descent. The temperature beta is GSE's aggressiveness dial. The book's warning that no automated tuning exists means GSE must calibrate beta per game situation, not assume a universal schedule.
verbatim_quote: The question is then how to balance the frequency of exploring and exploiting (i.e., greedy) actions.

title: Szepesvari-2010-AlgorithmsForReinforcementLearning
think: The Foundry now has its neurons (Nielsen), its deep representations (Prince), its fleet (Reddi), its in-game online constitution (Shalev-Shwartz 2012), and its pre-game generalization epistemology (Shalev-Shwartz & Ben-David 2014). Szepesvari's monograph supplies the missing decision layer: reinforcement learning, the theory of an agent that learns to ACT, not merely to predict. This is the layer that turns GSE from a calibrated forecaster into a play-caller. The football game is a Markov Decision Process: the state is down, distance, field position, formation, personnel, score and time; the action is the play or coverage call; the transition kernel is the stochastic outcome of that call. The decisive identification is that the 10,000-world crucible simulator IS an empirical estimate of the transition kernel P0. Every world the crucible rolls is a sample from P0(.|x,a), and the ensemble's average is the expected return the MDP theory optimizes. The objective is the discounted return, immediate EPA plus gamma-discounted future win-probability, and gamma is GSE's tempo dial — how much a play's future consequences weigh against its immediate gain. The value function V*(x) is the win-probability of a game state under optimal play-calling, and the action-value Q*(x,a) is the value of a specific call. The Bellman equation is the crucible's recursive evaluation rule: the value of a state is the immediate reward plus the discounted value of the resulting state, maximized over calls. Because the Bellman operators are maximum-norm contractions for gamma<1, the crucible's backward induction converges geometrically to a UNIQUE value surface — Banach's fixed-point theorem is the convergence guarantee of the whole simulation. Value iteration is that backward induction; policy iteration is the alternate refine-the-playbook loop (evaluate the current playbook, then improve it greedily). The Singh-Yee bound quantifies the stakes: a Q-estimation error of eps costs at most 2eps/(1-gamma) in policy value, so as gamma approaches one GSE must tighten its value accuracy or the play-call suboptimality blows up. The learning algorithms are how GSE acquires these values from data. Temporal-difference learning bootstraps — it uses its own predictions as targets — and the TD error, realized reward plus discounted next-state estimate minus current estimate, is exactly GSE's calibration surprise signal, updated snap-by-snap without waiting for the drive to end. TD is a stochastic-approximation algorithm tracking a stable linear ODE whose fixed point is the true value, and the Robbins-Monro step-size conditions are GSE's convergence contract; the book's warning that constant step-sizes give convergence in distribution (persistent variance) is GSE's calibration-jitter floor when tracking a shifting defense. TD(lambda) with eligibility traces is GSE's drive-level credit assignment: a touchdown's reward flows back across the drive's plays, and lambda controls how far back the credit reaches. Because the game-state space is enormous, the value function must be approximated as V_theta(x)=theta^T phi(x), where phi is the football ontology's feature map — the same inductive bias the PAC layer demanded — and averager-style features keep the learner max-norm well-behaved against the deadly triad of bootstrapping, off-policy sampling, and function approximation. Q-learning is the crown of the control layer. Its key insight is structural: the optimal ACTION-value is an expectation (the sup sits inside), so it can be estimated incrementally from sampled outcomes, whereas the optimal STATE-value has the sup outside and cannot. Q-learning is inherently OFF-POLICY — its max backup learns the value of the best call WOULD have been even when a different call was made. This is precisely how GSE mines decades of game film: it recovers optimal play values from the plays actually called, recovering the counterfactual the bandit layer said was unobservable. The price is the infinite-visitation condition: every state-action pair must be tried infinitely often, which makes exploration mandatory. Post-decision states (afterstates) are GSE's compute saving: learn the value of the resulting down-distance before the next stochastic event, and greedy action selection avoids a nested stochastic optimization. Finally, exploration. A pure-greedy learner can lock onto a suboptimal action with positive probability and incur large loss — the formal death of the tout's 'lock'. GSE must probe non-greedy calls, and the principled way is optimism in the face of uncertainty: UCB1 adds an uncertainty bonus R sqrt(2 log t / n_t) that is larger for less-tried calls, so the crucible automatically explores the whole playbook. The Boltzmann/softmax play-call distribution over Q-values is the SAME entropic link function as the online layer's mirror descent, tying the decision layer back to the regret layer. The RLVR reward verifier closes the loop by checking the Bellman residual T*Q-Q as a consistency gate: a learned play-value surface that violates its own Bellman equation is refused, not published. One more distinction organizes the whole layer. GSE runs BOTH a model-based and a model-free learner: the crucible is model-based (it simulates the transition kernel and plans by value iteration), while Q-learning on historical film is model-free (it estimates action-values directly from sampled transitions without ever building P0). The two must agree — a model-free Q-surface that contradicts the model-based crucible values signals a misspecified kernel or a non-stationary defense, and the disagreement is itself a calibration diagnostic. The actor-critic methods, the learned counterpart of policy iteration, split this into a critic that estimates value and an actor that improves the policy on a slower timescale, which is how GSE can refine its playbook online without re-running the full crucible at every snap. Every equation is a load-bearing law of GSE's play-call decision engine, the layer that turns calibrated prediction into optimal action.
theory_of_mind: Recursive theory of mind: an MDP is a theory-of-mind game against Nature. The transition kernel P0 is Nature's stochastic response to the agent's action; the agent models P0 to predict the consequences of its calls, and the value function is the agent's model of how its own future decisions will compound. In football the recursion is literal: the offense models the defense's coverage response to a call, the defense models the offense's tendency, and the engine models both — the Bellman backup nests these models recursively over the game tree. Off-policy Q-learning is a theory-of-mind superpower: it reasons about what the best call WOULD have been (the greedy target) while observing what was actually called (the behavior), exactly the counterfactual reasoning the bandit layer flagged as the hard part of partial feedback.
cross_layer_veto: Cross-layer veto adjudication: the online layer (2012) VETOES treating the in-game sequence as i.i.d. — the MDP transition kernel, not a fixed distribution, governs it. The PAC layer (2014) VETOES an unbounded-complexity value function class and demands the ontology features as inductive bias. The contraction layer VETOES gamma=1 value iteration without episodic structure (no contraction, no unique fixed point) and VETOES loose value accuracy as gamma->1 (the 2/(1-gamma) amplification). The Q-learning layer VETOES claiming convergence without infinite state-action visitation, and VETOES the deadly-triad combination (bootstrapping + off-policy + function approximation) without a well-behaved architecture. The exploration layer VETOES pure-greedy play-calling (positive-probability lock-on). The RLVR verifier VETOES any learned Q-surface with a nonzero Bellman residual T*Q-Q. When layers conflict the binding constraint wins and the gatekeeper PASSes rather than fabricating a guarantee: an unconverged value surface is refused, not published. Same fail-closed discipline as the pick-publication gate.

title: An Improved Adjusted Plus-Minus Statistic for NHL Players
primitive_name: Raw plus/minus is team- and opponent-dependent
gse_mapping: GSE context confound IS this plus/minus problem: the engine's raw on-field outcome for a factor is contaminated by co-active teammates, opponents, and situation, so individual contribution must be isolated by adjustment. GSI: component output confounded by system and environment.
verbatim_quote: a player's plus-minus is highly dependent on the team he plays for, the opponents he faces, and other variables out of his control, so it is not always a good measure of that player's individual contribution to his team.

title: An Improved Adjusted Plus-Minus Statistic for NHL Players
primitive_name: APM isolates contribution independent of teammates/opponents
gse_mapping: GSE confound-adjusted attribution IS APM: the engine regresses outcomes on factor-presence indicators controlling for all co-active factors, so each factor's coefficient is its marginal contribution independent of context. GSI: marginal attribution via regression on collinear presence indicators.
verbatim_quote: each player's APM is independent of the strength of that player's teammates and opponents.

title: An Improved Adjusted Plus-Minus Statistic for NHL Players
primitive_name: Good teammates raise, good opponents lower raw +/-

However, when cerebral compliance declines and elastance rises after a critical volume is reached in the intra- cranial compartment, this leads to greater changes in ICP and less changes in volume.

The Jarrahi review (reprint pp29-71) separates primary mechanical insult from secondary injury, and the secondary phase is where the mathematics lives: mechanical stretch opens micropores, sodium floods in, Na+/K+ ATPases fail as ATP collapses, depolarization dumps glutamate, NMDAR overactivation admits calcium, and calcium recruits proteases and radical chemistry (p33). Each step recruits the next; the system has positive feedback built into its ion gradients. The lipid peroxidation chain on p41 is the cleanest formal instance: AA + R• -> AA• + RH initiates, AA• + O2 -> AAOO• propagates, and AAOO• + AA -> AAOH + AA• regenerates the radical. One initiation event therefore damages many lipid molecules before termination; the chain length nu = propagation rate over initiation rate is the amplification factor. I deliberately keep nu symbolic because the source prints mechanism, not rate constants; assigning numeric k values from memory would launder external numbers into a source-anchored artifact. The same review supplies the termination side: GSH, SOD, CAT, GPx, the Nrf2-ARE inducible program (pp38, 42). The invariant is a race between initiation and termination capacity, and the clinical history in the review is exactly what happens when you lose that race at scale: PEG-SOD phase II succeeded with administration at 4 h post-injury while phase III failed at 8 h (p39), and NOS inhibitors protected only within one hour (p40). The therapeutic window is not a pharmacological footnote; it is the time constant of the cascade. An antioxidant that arrives after the chain has consumed its substrate budget cannot show effect, which is why the review insists on the 4-h difference between the two PEG-SOD trials. The Cheng stretch chapter (pp72-88) then gives the dose axis of the same cascade. Strain is the control parameter: 5% elongation supports survival and even enhances synaptic-vesicle velocity, 25% at 1 Hz for 6-24 h produces a sublethal stress phenotype (MMP depolarization at 6 h, 8-OHdG DNA damage and dopamine loss at 24 h, BDNF down, amyloid-beta and p-TauS396 up, GSK-3beta-tau complex formation), and 50% releases LDH and kills cells (p73). This is a regime map, not a linear dose-response: the same input channel produces adaptation, chronic stress, or death depending on amplitude. Two honesty flags belong in the record. First, the 5% and 50% anchors are cited prior work, not measurements of this paper. Second, the paper contradicts itself on geometry: Methods says biaxial stretch (p74), Results says uniaxial (pp75-79). Uniaxial and biaxial strain states are different stress tensors, so the effective dose is ambiguous; I extract the regime structure and flag the inconsistency rather than silently averaging it away. The authors' own limitation - proliferative SH-SY5Y cells are not terminally differentiated neurons (p84) - further bounds transfer. The MitoQ chapter (pp345-368) supplies the intervention side and the deepest structural insight of the book. MitoQ is ubiquinone conjugated to a lipophilic triphenylphosphonium cation; the cation accumulates at the inner mitochondrial membrane because of the electrochemical potential (p347). Formalizing that statement with the Nernst relation gives a concentration ratio exp(F*Delta psi/RT), roughly tenfold per 61.5 mV at body temperature - a derived kernel, explicitly labeled, since the source prints no equation. The paradox emerges when the chapters are read against each other: the stretch chapter shows injury depolarizes mitochondria (JC-1 green/red rises), and the Nernst kernel says accumulation collapses as the potential collapses. The delivery mechanism is gated by the very state variable the disease destroys. This is not a defect of MitoQ alone; it is a structural property of any state-dependent targeting scheme, and it explains why the effective dose in the cited prior work was 8 mg/kg while 2 mg/kg did nothing (p362), and why behavioral gains in the present study appear at 7 and 30 days but not day 3 (p352): the chronic window is where surviving, still-polarized mitochondria can be rescued and the inflammatory loop dampened. Connecting the three primitives yields one coherent operator picture of secondary injury: a strain-dose sets the regime (p3), the regime ignites chain-amplified damage (p1), and any repair intervention carries a state-dependent delivery kernel (p4). The football translation is an isomorphism of structure, not a fabricated origin: a defense is also a cascade system where one broken assignment propagates through adjacent defenders until a termination event, where load regimes separate adaptation from injury, and where a corrective install only takes hold in units whose execution potential is intact. The calibration discipline is identical on both sides: measure the amplification ratio, the regime boundaries, and the delivery gradient before claiming an intervention effect. The book's own translational failures - CRASH corticosteroids increasing mortality (p45), progesterone phase III null (p50), more than 30 failed phase III trials in three decades (p346) - are the empirical scar tissue proving that single-target, late-arriving, state-blind interventions lose to cascades. That is the durable lesson this artifact carries forward: cascades are beaten by termination capacity and timing, not by stronger single pushes.

The clinician's comfort call is stabilization: control ICP, prevent seizures, discharge on symptom absence - a policy optimized for the observable acute state. The molecular researcher's belief is that the real game is the invisible secondary cascade, so symptom absence is not clearance; the 24-h biomarker latency in the stretch model is her evidence. think: The second sovereign theme of this reprint is that measurement is not a window but a construction, and the construction can fail in structured, predictable ways. Three independent instances in the book form a single operator family. Instance one is the ddPCR normalization pipeline (pp96-97). Droplet digital PCR returns absolute copy numbers, but the raw count per well still carries two nuisance scales: how much RNA went into the cDNA reaction, and how efficiently the sample was processed. The printed pipeline removes them in two quotients: first divide average copies per 20 uL well by the total RNA input to the 15 uL cDNA reaction (computed from NanoDrop concentration and the 1:100 dilution), then divide by the geometric mean of four endogenous controls (miR-378a-3p, miR-3594-3p, miR-330-5p, let-7b-3p). Algebraically this is a projection onto a quotient space: each sample carries an unknown positive multiplicative factor s, the observable is s times the true abundance, and dividing by invariant references makes s act trivially. The geometric mean is the correct aggregator because the nuisance is multiplicative and approximately log-normal; an arithmetic mean would let one high-count control dominate. The same paper runs the identical construction at sequencing scale with TMM normalization (p95) and at qPCR scale with 2^-DeltaCt (p97, Livak-Schmittgen lineage). Recognizing all three as one gauge-fixing operator is the extraction's value: the invariant is not the miRNA biology but the normalization structure, and it transfers to any rate statistic where opportunity volume is the nuisance scale. The breakdown is equally structural: if a reference is itself regulated, the quotient injects the biology it was supposed to remove. The book guards this with RIN 8.9-9.2 and 260/280 ratios 2.01-2.10 (p94) and by selecting controls from non-differential sequencing results - but the guard is an assumption, not a theorem. Instance two is canonical-probe blindness (p105), the most elegant measurement failure in the book. The miR-146a locus produces a distribution of isoforms; the canonical miRBase sequence is one coordinate of that distribution. After TBI the canonical fraction of aligned reads falls from 48.32% to 37.71% while 3'-added isomiRs rise. A primer assay targeting only the canonical sequence reports FC=1.4, p>0.05 - nothing. An assay detecting all 3'-end isomiRs reports FC=1.7, p<0.05 - a real effect. The canonical assay is a lossy projection pi onto one coordinate; the effect lives in the complement, so the projection is not merely noisy but systematically blind, and can even trend opposite to the full signal because the canonical share shrinks while the locus total grows. The functional consequence is not cosmetic: the full miR-146a profile (canonical plus all isomiRs) correlates with worse 3-month neuroscore at Spearman r=0.75 (p109), and the 3'tRFs correlate even more strongly (r=0.78 and r=0.92). A research program that had trusted the canonical-only assay would have discarded miR-146a as unchanged and never reached the behavioral coupling. The measurement choice determined which biology was discoverable. The source also bounds the isoform assay itself: 3' additions have 'diverse and contradictory functions' (p111), low-abundance miR-155-5p yields no isomiRs and drops out (p97), and the 5% retention threshold (p95) censors rare variants - so the summed isoform count is a better coordinate, not a final truth. Instance three is the loading-control hazard in the Yoshida chapter (p268). Mitochondrial Western blots are normalized to COX-IV, but the authors explicitly warn that COX-IV may itself be damaged in AD transgenic mice, so the denominator of the normalization is condition-dependent. This is instance one's breakdown realized in print: when the reference frame is damaged by the disease, every normalized ratio inherits a spurious shift. The authors recommend multiple loading proteins - a direct admission that a single gauge is unsafe when the gauge itself is a state variable. The hippocampal findings (SOD-2 down, 3-NT up, NMNAT-3 down, NQO-1 collapsing between 3 and 6 months while cortical NQO-1 stays elevated) are therefore extracted with the normalization caveat attached, not as raw truth. Synthesizing: the book's measurement doctrine is (1) choose references that are invariant under the condition, (2) aggregate multiplicatively with geometric means, (3) choose the measurement coordinate to span where the effect lives, and (4) audit whether the reference itself is a state variable. The football isomorphism is immediate and non-fabricated: headline stats are canonical projections of scheme-dependent behavior distributions; per-snap and per-possession rates are gauge-fixing quotients; and a scouting reference (a baseline opponent, a replacement-level comparator) that is itself affected by the scheme being studied reproduces the COX-IV hazard exactly. The deception layer follows: an opponent who knows you scout the canonical coordinate can present a canonical profile that hides the isoform tail - the statistical analog of showing a base formation while the effect lives in the motion split. The durable invariant is that every comparison carries a gauge, every gauge can be captured by the condition, and every projection can be gamed; the audit is to name the gauge, test its invariance, and locate the effect before trusting the number.

The assay designer believes the canonical sequence IS the target - a belief inherited from the miRBase catalog - and designs primers to it. The biologist believes the functional entity is the isoform distribution, because 3' additions change folding and Argonaute association (p105, p111). The statistician believes any comparison is only as good as its reference invariance, and watches the COX-IV warning (p268) with alarm. title: 203aeb745b1aed40
gse_mapping: Derived coverage-taxonomy kernel: cluster opponent plays (features = formation, motion, personnel, down/distance) into K coverage families. The theorem guarantees the staff's iterative taxonomy refinement terminates, but only at a local optimum — two staffs starting from different initial film sessions can carve the same opponent into different, equally self-consistent taxonomies. title: 203aeb745b1aed40
think:
The invariant that organizes this entire book is the gap between two quantities: the training error epsilon-hat that we can compute, and the expected loss epsilon over the unknown distribution D that we actually care about (p. 16). Every algorithm in the text is a bridge across that gap, and every failure mode is a bridge collapse. The decision-tree chapter makes the collapse concrete: a fully grown tree achieves lower training error but higher test error than a pruned tree (p. 19). Memorization is not learning. This is the first veto the book hands us: any GSE model scored on the games it was fit on is measuring epsilon-hat, not epsilon, and the doctrine 'never touch your test data' (p. 21) is the operational form of that veto.

The perceptron gives the gap a quantitative shape. Theorem 1 (p. 45) says that if the data are linearly separable with margin gamma and all inputs satisfy ||x|| <= 1, then error-driven updates converge after at most 1/gamma-squared mistakes. Read carefully, the bound is a statement about an adaptation budget: the number of corrections needed is controlled by how cleanly the classes separate, not by the number of examples seen. The proof's telescoping argument — the weight vector's projection onto the optimal separator grows by at least gamma per mistake while its norm grows by at most one — is a conservation-law-style reasoning: progress is bounded by geometry. But the theorem also carries two scars. First, convergence is guaranteed only under separability; on non-separable data the algorithm can oscillate forever (the bias-only example, p. 43). Second, the perceptron is indifferent to margin quality: it may return a separator of margin 0.000001 on data separable at margin 0.9 (p. 46). The SVM chapter exists precisely to repair that second scar.

Transferring this to the 22-player system as a derived kernel: each play is an example whose features are normalized formation, motion, and personnel descriptors (the normalization pipeline on pp. 55-56 is what makes ||x|| <= 1 literally true), and whose label is the observed coverage outcome. A coaching staff's tendency classifier that updates only on mispredicted plays inherits the bound: at most 1/gamma-squared corrective plays are needed when the opponent's tendencies separate with margin gamma. Ambiguous formations — trips bunch versus condensed split, where two coverages are nearly confusable — have small gamma and provably demand more film. The bound also tells us when to stop trusting the classifier: if the opponent changes coordinator at halftime, the fixed-margin witness w* no longer exists for the new distribution, and the convergence guarantee evaporates exactly when a staff most needs it. The i.i.d. assumption the book calls 'usually false but sufficiently close' (p. 103) is, in football, sometimes catastrophically false within a single game. Finally, the cross-validation warning on p. 62 — split by image, not by pixel — dictates the held-out unit: whole games, never individual plays, because plays within a game are correlated draws.
theory_of_mind: Three belief systems collide on every snap. The head coach models the defensive coordinator as a stationary tendency distribution — 'they play Cover 3 on early downs' — and calls his comfort play against that model. The DC knows the coach holds that model and deliberately feeds it: he shows Cover 3 leverage pre-snap and rotates late, so the coach's classifier is trained on deception. The quarterback carries a third, faster model — his internal clock believes the window closes in under three seconds, so he throws before the post-snap evidence resolves. Each agent is modeling the others' models, and the play's outcome is the fixed point of that recursion, not the argmax of any single classifier.
cross_layer_veto: The classifier's margin says the deep post is open: single-high safety, large gamma, high expected value. Physiology vetoes. Late in the fourth quarter the quarterback's shoulder is fatigued — bioenergetic depletion lengthens his release, and the offensive line's pass-rush win rate has collapsed, so the pocket the margin was computed under no longer exists. The realized gamma shrinks below the regime where the bound is useful, and the remaining plays on the clock are fewer than the 1/gamma-squared adaptation budget the error-driven update would need. The high-EV call is rejected not because the model is wrong but because its assumptions have expired mid-game.

title: 203aeb745b1aed40
think:
If the perceptron chapter bounds how fast we can learn, the Bayes-optimal chapter bounds how well anyone can ever do. Theorem 8 (p. 101) says that if we knew the true distribution D, the classifier that returns argmax over labels of D(x-hat, y-hat) achieves minimal zero/one error among all deterministic classifiers. The corollary is the Bayes error: the irreducible floor of the task. The book's label-noise example (pp. 139-140) makes it visceral — if twenty percent of labels are coin flips, no algorithm, however clever, can beat that floor. This is the second veto: any GSE projection claiming accuracy above the estimated irreducible variance of repeated identical situations is claiming to beat the Bayes error, which means it is leaking, overfitting, or lying. The floor itself is latent — unidentifiable from finite samples — so we can only upper-bound it with the best held-out error we achieve, and calibrate it from outcome variance across near-identical down/distance/formation/personnel situations.

But D is never known. The generative chapters show what we do instead: we invent a story about how the data were produced and fit its parameters. Naive Bayes (p. 105) assumes words are conditionally independent given the label — an assumption the book admits is false, since 'the' and 'and' co-occur constantly — yet the classifier works because the decision boundary can be right even when the probability model is wrong. That is a profound engineering lesson: a model's assumptions are a bet about which errors are tolerable, not a claim of literal truth. The SVM's slack variables make the same bet explicit. Equation 6.45 (p. 99) shows the optimal slack on an example is exactly its hinge loss, so the soft-margin objective (1/2)||w||^2 + C times the sum of hinge losses is a single dial — C — controlling how much one noisy play may move the staff's belief. A blown assignment that does not reflect the called coverage is label noise; large C forces the model to contort around it, small C lets it slide. The support vectors, where alpha_n > 0 (KKT condition, p. 136), are exactly the boundary formations where two coverages are confusable — the deception frontier.

Unsupervised learning removes the labels and the floor with them. K-means (Theorem 15, p. 164) converges in finitely many iterations because both steps — nearest-centroid assignment and mean re-estimation — can only decrease the sum-of-squares objective L, which is bounded below by zero. But convergence is only to a local optimum. Two staffs starting from different initial film sessions can carve the same opponent into different, equally self-consistent coverage taxonomies, and the theorem offers no way to prefer one. The book's own advice is to run it ten times with different initializations and keep the best L (p. 164); K-means++ (Theorem 16, p. 166) upgrades that heuristic to a guarantee, E[L-hat] <= 8(log K + 2) L-opt. EM (p. 172) then softens the hard assignments: a disguised coverage is not Cover 3 or Cover 1 but a fractional responsibility over both, and the Jensen lower-bound argument (p. 175) shows we can optimize a touching bound on the true likelihood instead of the intractable log-sum. The through-line: every layer of the book replaces an intractable ideal — known D, global optimum, hard truth — with a tractable surrogate, and the discipline is knowing exactly what the surrogate gave up.
theory_of_mind: The defensive coordinator's disguise is a theory-of-mind weapon aimed at the quarterback's read heuristic. The QB reads coverage pre-snap like a naive Bayes classifier: safety depth, corner leverage, and linebacker width treated as independent evidence. The DC knows this and exploits the conditional dependence — under a disguised look those features are correlated by design, so the QB's independent-evidence sum overconfirms the wrong coverage. A QB who models the DC's intent ('they want me to think Cover 2') must hold a soft, EM-style belief over coverages and collapse it only on post-snap movement. The disguise wins exactly when the QB hard-assigns too early.
cross_layer_veto: A slate optimizer loves a high-variance stack justified by a clustering of game scripts. The veto is structural: K-means converges only to a local optimum, so the 'game script cluster' the stack's correlation structure rests on is initialization-dependent — an early touchdown against the script can flip the assignment and invalidate the entire correlation model mid-slate. Physiology compounds it: accumulated collision workload changes player outcome distributions across a season, violating the stationarity the clustering assumed. The tail-risk position is rejected because its foundational partition is a local optimum masquerading as ground truth.

gse_mapping: Role-specific marginal value decay: define the drop in expected points between adjacent within-role ranks; draft priority should be ordered by relative decay (value over the next-best alternative at the same role), not by absolute expected points. This is the value-over-replacement kernel that justifies waiting on QB/K/DS and prioritizing scarce RB/WR/TE slots, and it binds as the resource-valuation layer of any sequential competitive allocation sim.

title: 21544db09ed29308
think: Lee and Liu treat the fantasy draft as a canonical sequential competitive decision task, and the decomposition they give is the sovereign object: repeated preferential choice among uncertain-valued resources under roster constraints, plus prediction of opponents who deplete the same pool. The first component is a constrained sequential allocation problem, cousin to bandits, optimal stopping, and stochastic knapsacks; the second is adversarial theory of mind. The paper's central methodological move is to refuse the normative shortcut: prior draft-optimization work assumed fixed opponent strategies without fitting behavior, and this study measures behavior first. The environment analysis supplies the valuation kernel. Role-specific point decay is sharply heterogeneous: the best-to-fifth gap is 119 points for running backs, 77 for wide receivers, 138 for tight ends, but only 30 for quarterbacks, 19 for kickers, 10 for defenses, with near-linear tails afterward. Because the objective is the probability of outscoring an opponent rather than absolute points, the correct priority ordering follows relative decay, which is why waiting on quarterback, kicker, and defense is rational even though quarterbacks score the most absolute points. The calibration evidence bounds how much skill the task can carry: draft position correlates with realized points at r = -0.56 for running backs and -0.55 for wide receivers, -0.88 for kickers, but only -0.21 for quarterbacks, -0.17 for tight ends, and +0.22 for defenses, consistent with defense scoring being highly unpredictable. So the environment is partially knowable, and the knowable part is concentrated in the scarce roles. The measurement regime must travel with every kernel: 1350 sleeper.app leagues from the 2017 NFL season, 12,590 teams of which 11,932 are human, 188,426 human selections of which 27 percent are auto-picks and are excluded from the strategy analyses; bot teams won only 39 percent of games against 51 percent for humans, which is itself a calibration anchor. Roster sizes 14 to 20, league sizes 6 to 12, serpentine order, PPR scoring. Three breakdown regimes follow. First, single-season single-platform scope: the authors themselves flag the draft-position winning anomaly (first pick performing poorly) as too season-idiosyncratic to interpret without replication, and the same caution applies to every composition result. Second, scoring-regime dependence: the gradients are PPR averages over 2015 to 2020, and a different scoring system reweights roles. Third, the auto-pick contamination: more than a quarter of human-team selections are algorithmic, so any behavioral kernel estimated without excluding them mixes human and machine policies. The extraction therefore carries the scarcity gradient, the relative objective, and the calibration table as one interlocking valuation layer, with all three regimes declared.
theory_of_mind: The draft is a recursion of beliefs: each manager models what the next manager will take, and the serpentine structure varies how many opponent picks intervene between one's own, so the required lookahead depth differs by draft seat. The paper connects this to level-k models: if people cannot look ahead past the intervening picks, middle seats and end seats face different cognitive loads. The observed herding is the failure mode of that recursion, where instead of modeling the opponent's plan, the agent copies the opponent's last action. Expert advice models the environment but not the opponents, which is exactly the missing recursive layer.
cross_layer_veto: Three vetoes bind. The measurement layer vetoes any behavioral claim estimated with auto-picks included, since 27 percent of human-team selections are algorithmic and would contaminate the policy mixture. The replication layer vetoes interpreting the first-pick winning anomaly or any single-season composition edge as a law; the authors themselves demand cross-season replication first. And the objective layer vetoes expected-points maximization as a stand-in for winning: because success is P(outscore), a higher-mean lower-variance roster can be the wrong call when the variance posture is wrong, so any high-EV draft recommendation must be re-scored under the joint distribution, not the mean.

title: 21544db09ed29308
think: The strategy-level results are mostly disciplined nulls, and the nulls are the sovereign content because each comes with an explicit test and effect-size prior. Handcuffing, the promoted injury-insurance strategy, fails both tests: usage counts of same-team co-drafts mostly sit at chance expectation given league size, and the 793 handcuffing teams won 51.04 percent against 50.56 percent for non-handcuffing teams, a Bayes factor of 4.2 for sameness under a Gaussian effect-size prior with mean zero and standard deviation 0.1. The apparent usage excesses dissolve under the backup-only logic: Elliott-McFadden and Martin-Rodgers are pairs of frequently drafted players, not insurance legs. Favorite-NFL-team stacking fails too: observed same-team count distributions match chance base rates for all 32 teams, so the correlated-asset variance instrument exists as a rational option but is not exercised, and the authors note the variance rationale is only sensible for expected-score underdogs. What does survive is implicit: the preceding-pick influence, where conditional role-choice probability exceeds the base rate for early quarterbacks and nearly all kicker and defense picks, while running back, wide receiver, and tight end choices are unaffected. Crucially this bias is performance-neutral, with Bayes factors for sameness of 4.7, 5.7, and 8.8, so it is a predictable pattern without a measurable cost, which is precisely what makes it exploitable rather than merely pathological. The composition analysis adds the representativeness interpretation: rosters are built to resemble the salient active-roster template, the five most common compositions win close to half their games, and eight fringe compositions win clearly more, all emphasizing running backs and wide receivers over kickers and defenses. The authors then impose the robustness criterion from the evolution-of-strategies literature: no strategy is guaranteed optimal because effectiveness depends on the league's strategy distribution; a good strategy must be robust across plausible opponent distributions and stable under universalization. For the GSE Coach-Mind simulation this composes into a concrete opponent-model upgrade: replace fixed normative opponent assumptions with the measured cumulative role-order distributions, add the role- and stage-specific herding term, and evaluate any policy against a distribution of opponent compositions with the universalization stability test. The paper's own application section says exactly this: the herding regularity is an opening for exploitation. For GSI the binding is structural, not physiological: sequential competitive allocation of scarce uncertain-valued resources under a legality constraint is the same task family as scarce-slot clinical scheduling, and the representativeness failure, confusing the constraint pattern with the objective, is the same failure as protocol-shaped compliance that misses the outcome target. Doctrine holds throughout: the observables here are fantasy points, draft positions, and winning proportions, never sportsbook odds, and no result is promoted to a win-rate headline; the 2017 single-season window is a cutoff to respect, and every kernel carries its Bayes prior and its replication veto.
theory_of_mind: Recursive belief clash is measurable here. The expert-advice follower believes the template is optimal because it matches the active-roster concept; the fringe strategist believes the crowd's representativeness is exploitable; the herding manager does not model beliefs at all and simply copies the last pick. Under draft pressure, the comfort call is the template pick, because deviating is socially detectable, the paper notes that failing to draft a kicker or defense would quickly be flagged as unusual. The optimizer's theory of mind must therefore model two opponent classes, template-followers and copycats, and the paper's measured distributions give the mixture weights directly.
cross_layer_veto: The Bayesian layer vetoes declaring handcuffing or copying harmful or helpful: Bayes factors of 4.2 to 8.8 for sameness support the null under the stated priors, and flipping them requires new data, not reinterpretation. The game-theoretic layer vetoes promoting any fringe composition to a recommended strategy without the universalization test, because its edge is defined against the current opponent distribution and may die when adopted. And the scope layer vetoes transporting 2017 sleeper.app kernels to other platforms, seasons, or scoring regimes without re-estimation; the authors' own replication demand on the draft-position anomaly is the template for that veto.

The counterintuitive headline is that the deviance coefficient is negative and marginally significant, minus 0.044 at p equals 0.053, meaning more reported misconduct was associated with being drafted higher under the original Tagliabue policy, roughly a 4.4 percent improvement per additional reported incident, while the deviance-by-Goodell interaction is insignificant at p equals 0.597, so the advantage vanishes under the modified policy.

think: Machine Learning Yearning is not a book of theorems; it is a book of diagnostics, and its deepest invariant is that every improvement lever must be selected by reading the error structure of the current system, not by intuition. Ng opens with the cat-startup scenario precisely because the failure mode is universal: a team under pressure holds a menu of plausible directions - more data, a bigger network, more training iterations, regularization - and no principled way to choose. The book's answer is a decomposition. Dev error splits into the training error (informally, bias) and the gap between dev and training error (informally, variance); once an estimate of the optimal error rate exists, bias splits again into unavoidable bias (the Bayes floor) and avoidable bias. Each cell of that decomposition licenses a different intervention, and the wrong intervention is not merely useless but actively wasteful: adding data to a high-bias system makes the training problem harder without touching the bottleneck. The learning-curve chapters turn this into a visual extrapolation discipline - if the training-error curve already sits above the desired performance and can only rise with more data, then no amount of data collection can reach the goal, and months of collection are vetoed before they are spent. For the GSE model stack this is the triage kernel we have been missing. Our play-outcome models are trained on logged plays from past seasons and evaluated on the current one, so the basic same-distribution assumption is violated by construction. Ng's chapters 40-41 supply the exact repair: hold out a Training-dev set drawn from the training distribution, and read the three errors - training, training-dev, dev - as a syndrome. A small training error with a large training-dev error is variance; a large training error is avoidable bias; a small gap within the training distribution but a large jump to the dev distribution is data mismatch, which is what an era shift looks like when rule changes or schematic evolution move the underlying distribution. The decomposition tells us whether to spend the next wave on more seasons of data, on a bigger model, or on era-matched reweighting - and the beta-weighting idea from chapter 39 (give the out-of-distribution bulk a lower weight, beta=1/40 in the worked example) is the cheap compromise when compute cannot afford to model both distributions fully. Two further disciplines bind directly to our held-out doctrine. First, the Eyeball/Blackbox dev split: the portion of the dev set an analyst manually reviews overfits faster, so a divergence between Eyeball and Blackbox performance is the alarm that the review process itself is contaminating the estimate. That is exactly the mechanism our sealed-baseline discipline guards against, and Ng gives us the detector, not just the rule. Second, the mislabeling analysis: when the system is at 10% error, 0.6% of label noise is tolerable; at 2% error the same 0.6% is 30% of all remaining error and must be cleaned - and cleaned on dev and test together, or the same-distribution invariant breaks. The ceiling argument of chapter 14 completes the loop: before any feature is built, count the fraction of errors it could possibly address, because that fraction times the current error is the maximum it can ever buy. A month of engineering for a 0.5-point ceiling is a vetoed investment, and the veto is quantitative, not political. The human-level chapters add the calibration anchor: use the best available human proxy (the team-of-doctors 2% example, not the junior doctor's 10%) as the estimate of the optimal error rate, because any weaker proxy is necessarily too high and will mislabel avoidable bias as unavoidable. For football, the analogous proxy is expert-consensus grading on charted plays, and its error rate is the floor below which our models cannot meaningfully be pushed. Everything above that floor is engineering; everything at it is the irreducible randomness of twenty-two coupled agents, and the honest response to it is variance reduction and better constraints, not pretending the floor can be broken.
theory_of_mind: Under pressure the coach defaults to the comfort call - run up the middle on third-and-long because it feels safe - while the defensive coordinator models that comfort and stacks the box, and the quarterback's internal clock, shortened by anticipated pressure, vetoes the very reads the comfort call depends on. Each agent is modeling the others recursively. Ng's single-number metric is a device for breaking that hall of mirrors: it replaces private intuition with a shared ordering, so the coach, the coordinator, and the analyst argue about one number instead of three incommensurable beliefs.
cross_layer_veto: Even when the win-probability model ranks a deep shot highest, physiology and clock physics veto it: the quarterback's time-to-throw under pressure is bounded by rush arrival, fatigue accumulates across the game, and hit exposure compounds. The satisficing constraint - decision latency inside the play-clock window, workload inside the fatigue budget - dominates the optimizing metric. The veto is not a model failure; it is a constraint the model must internalize, exactly as Ng's wakeword system minimizes false negatives only subject to a hard false-positive cap.

title: 24cd6351f8d171a6
think: The second sovereign pattern in the book is the separation of scoring from search, and the Optimization Verification test is the instrument that keeps the two honest. Any system that learns an approximate Score_x(y) and then approximately maximizes it - speech recognition with beam search, machine translation, reinforcement learning over helicopter trajectories - can fail in two distinct ways, and the failure modes demand opposite investments. The test is a single computed inequality: score the known-superior reference output and the emitted output under the same scoring function. If the reference scores higher, the search failed to find what the model already knew was better; widen the beam, relax the pruning, improve the optimizer. If the reference does not score higher, the model itself is blind to the truth; no search improvement can help, and the learning algorithm must be refit. Ng's worked census - 95% of errors due to the scoring function, 5% to search - converts directly into a ceiling: perfecting the search eliminates at most 5% of errors. The Coach-Mind play-call engine is precisely this pattern. A win-probability-added model scores candidate plays from the current state, and a bounded search - constrained by clock, personnel, formation, and the fatigue budget - emits one call. When a reviewed snap shows the emitted call underperforming an expert reference call, we compute both scores and attribute the error. Over a census of such snaps we get the fraction of failures that live in the search versus the fraction that live in the transition kernel, and that fraction decides where the next wave of engineering goes. The reference need not be optimal - Ng's helicopter chapter explicitly allows a human-pilot trajectory that is merely superior - which matters because expert charted calls are available even where no provably optimal call exists. Error analysis by parts extends the same attribution logic to pipelines. The perfect-input substitution test - replace component A's output with a hand-labeled perfect output and rerun B and C - assigns each error to exactly one component along the DAG, and the generalization to A, B, C ordered by the directed acyclic graph means our perception-prediction-decision stack can be audited the same way. The crown jewel is the flawed-pipeline theorem of chapter 57: if every component is at human-level performance given its inputs, yet the whole system falls far short of human-level, the pipeline itself is flawed - the intermediate representation is discarding information the decision needs. The lane-markings example is the template: the fix is not a better planner but a new perception channel feeding the planner. For football, if our formation and personnel modules are each near expert-level yet the call engine underperforms, the missing channel is something like leverage, alignment, or motion intent, and the theorem tells us to add the channel rather than refit the planner. Finally, the metric-design chapters close the loop. F1's harmonic mean punishes imbalance, so a deception detector with high precision and low recall cannot hide behind its precision; and the optimizing/satisficing split forbids the dimensionally inhomogeneous blend of accuracy and latency into one score, forcing instead a constrained formulation whose thresholds are explicit and auditable. Together these give the sim a governance layer: one number to rank, one inequality to attribute blame, one ceiling to gate investment, and one constraint set to keep the whole thing inside the physical and physiological envelope of the actual game.
theory_of_mind: The analyst believes the model is wrong; the coach believes the play-selection logic is wrong; each discounts the other's evidence because neither can see inside the other's component. The Optimization Verification test is a belief-arbitration protocol: it replaces authority with a number both sides can compute. Recursive theory of mind enters on the scoring side - the model must represent the defensive coordinator's expectations about our tendencies - while the search side stays a bounded optimizer, keeping the two belief layers from contaminating each other.
cross_layer_veto: Information theory vetoes downstream investment when the pipeline's intermediate representation has already discarded what the decision needs: no planner, however good, can recover lane markings that were never perceived, and no play-caller can recover leverage that the formation module threw away. Psychology adds a second veto: an analyst who has manually reviewed a hundred plays overfits the Eyeball set, and a widening Eyeball-Blackbox gap forbids promoting that analyst's favored configuration until fresh data restores the gap.

title: 25294936f511d828
think: The Playfair case study is not a theorem book; it is a measurement-and-encoding report, and its sovereign content is a set of structural claims about the NFL's coaching labor market that can be lifted into the Foundry as kernels with explicit failure regimes. The central object is the reshuffling effect: the source states that white head coaching candidates receive second and third chances while candidates of color generally receive one. Read as a dynamical system, the head-coach population is a Markov-like renewal process over states {employed, unemployed-but-eligible, exited}, and the claim is that the reentry transition probability P(rehire | fired) is group-dependent. That is a testable kernel, not a slogan: the data architecture on page 12 builds exactly the sufficient statistics for it, namely a new-head-coach flag, a first-time-coach flag, previous position, tenure value, and missing years. Tenure spells are the run-length encoding of this process, and the Pilula chart on page 15 is a lossless visual serialization of spell lengths: bar length equals total seasons filling the role, color encodes the self-reported racial category, rows are teams, and the x-axis is the season. The encoding choice matters because spell length is the observable from which a discrete-time firing hazard can be estimated; a team that cycles quickly through short spells has a high hazard, and the dashboard's stated purpose is to find exactly those teams. The second kernel is the proposed mechanism: implicit bias, which the source quotes from the NIH as automatic and unintentional yet effective on judgments, decisions, and behaviors. The crucial word is unintentionally: the decision-maker's self-model contains no bias term, so introspection cannot identify it. The only identification route is statistical, comparing hiring and reentry rates across groups conditional on resume observables (wins, losses, playoff appearances, years of NFL experience, previous position), which the pipeline explicitly joins. The source's own scoping decisions define the measurement regime: 1993 through 2023, thirty seasons, thirty-two teams, 168 head coaches and 149 general managers, with earlier records rejected as incomplete and inconsistent. That window is a stationarity assumption, not a law of nature: rules, franchise locations, and the coordinator-to-head-coach pipeline itself change inside it, and the team-renaming step (Oakland to Las Vegas) shows the engineers already had to repair identity continuity. Race is self-reported, which makes it a measurement channel with its own missingness and misclassification risk rather than ground truth. Three failure regimes must travel with these kernels. First, the Pilula figure in the case study carries an explicit disclaimer that its values are mere approximations for illustrative purposes, so no quantitative claim may be calibrated from the case-study artwork; only the published dashboard data could calibrate it. Second, the reshuffling claim as quoted is unconditional, it does not control for resume quality, so it is a disparity observation, not yet a bias estimate; the gap between those two is exactly where omitted-variable confounding lives. Third, the one-chance pattern for candidates of color means small effective sample sizes for group-specific reentry hazards; pooling across decades buys precision at the cost of the stationarity assumption. A sovereign extraction therefore records the kernel, its sufficient statistics, and all three vetoes, and refuses to upgrade the descriptive claim into a causal one without the conditional comparison.
theory_of_mind: Recursion runs through every hiring node. The GM models the owner's tolerance for a risky first-time hire; the owner models fan and media reaction; the candidate models whether his resume will even be read. Because the bias is automatic and unintentional by definition, each agent's self-model is sincerely meritocratic while the aggregate kernel is not, a belief clash that cannot be resolved by asking anyone their intentions. Under pressure the comfort call dominates: rehiring a known white retread is defensible in every recursive model because he has done the job before, while the equally qualified first-time candidate of color is risky in at least one layer. The dashboard is an intervention in this recursion: it gives each layer observable evidence about the others' actual behavior.
cross_layer_veto: Three vetoes travel with these kernels. The measurement layer vetoes any calibration from the case-study Pilula artwork, because the source explicitly labels its values illustrative approximations. The statistical layer vetoes upgrading the unconditional reshuffling disparity into a causal bias estimate without conditioning on wins, losses, experience, and previous position; omitted-variable confounding is not a footnote here, it is the whole gap. And the small-sample layer vetoes group-specific hazard estimates for candidates of color whose spells are mostly singletons; pooling is allowed only with the stationarity cost declared. A high-EV fire-and-rehire-the-retread call is vetoed by the pipeline-collapse dynamics: it is locally defensible and globally pool-destroying.

title: 25294936f511d828
think: The remaining kernels govern the information channel between the measurement and the action, and they are where this case study binds to the Coach-Mind simulation and to GSI telemetry. Slovic's compassion fade and psychic numbing, quoted on page 9, state that numbers without human connection lose their power to drive action: if readers do not relate to the information, they are less likely to act and use it. Formally this is a gain function on the information-to-action channel that decreases with aggregation level. The Playfair design response, drilling from team-and-role aggregates down to individual career journeys, is a channel-gain restoration strategy, and it is testable: the same disparity shown as a league aggregate versus as one named coach's resume should produce different action rates. The diffusion kernel from Rogers, quoted on page 4, closes the loop: new behaviors spread rapidly once a critical mass has adopted, which is a threshold contagion process. Applied to the case study's own goal of bias-free, merit-based hiring, the adoption fraction of teams using structured, objective criteria is the state variable, and the critical mass is the tipping point above which the practice self-propagates. Below it, each adopting team bears the full cost alone; above it, non-adopters face normative and competitive pressure. The conclusion on page 19 is consistent with this reading: sustainable change requires the selection process itself to become merit-based, not more dashboards. For the GSE Coach-Mind simulation, the composition is concrete. The 22-player dynamical system is nested inside a coaching labor market whose reentry kernel is group-asymmetric. Simulating coach quality draws without that asymmetry overstates the effective candidate pool: reshuffling recycles known quantities instead of injecting new talent, which reduces the variance of the quality distribution and fattens the left tail of long-run team performance, a portfolio tail-risk statement, not a win-rate headline. The simulation must therefore carry the hiring kernel as a constraint layer above the play-level system, with implicit bias as a latent offset in the selection utility and compassion fade as a gain on any feedback channel that is supposed to correct the offset. For GSI, the isomorphism is clinical: alarm fatigue and aggregate-versus-patient telemetry are the same channel-gain problem, a ward-level statistic does not move a clinician the way one identified patient's trajectory does, and implicit bias is the same latent-offset problem in triage and treatment decisions. The audit lens is identical in both institutes: find the latent offset, find the channel gain, find the adoption threshold, and demand telemetry at the level where action actually happens. The discipline constraints bind here too. The 1993-2023 window is the source's cutoff; any Foundry fit using these kernels must respect held-out discipline, no fit scored on its own training rows, no post-cutoff leakage, and no sportsbook odds anywhere in the pipeline. The case study's joins use wins, losses, and playoff appearances as performance covariates, which are legitimate observables; odds are not, and nothing in this extraction introduces them.
theory_of_mind: The audience model is explicit and recursive: Playfair assumes NFL fans with average data literacy, comfortable with line and bar charts but not treemaps, and designs downward to that model. The fan, in turn, models the coach as a person only when the data reaches individual level; above that, compassion fade numbs the response. The hiring decision-maker sits in the same loop: presented with league aggregates he sees a statistic, presented with one named coach's blocked resume he sees a person. The design insight is that theory of mind is not just for opponents, it is the specification of the information channel's receiver, and getting it wrong silently zeroes the channel gain.
cross_layer_veto: The psychology layer vetoes the high-EV communication call: an aggregate-only dashboard maximizes information density and minimizes action probability, so efficiency metrics that ignore compassion fade select the wrong design. The diffusion layer vetoes declaring victory at first adoption: below critical mass the practice dies with its champion, so a single team's bias-free hiring is not evidence of a regime change. And the doctrine layer vetoes any temptation to score these kernels with odds-derived labels or to fit them on their own training rows; the 1993-2023 window is a cutoff to respect, not a convenience to extend.

think: This book is a ladder from a pile of raw facts to a model, and the sovereign reading is that every rung adds an assumption that can break. The author opens by calling raw data 'the numerical equivalent of a pile of footballs' — more than the brain can hold — and defines analysis as compressing that pile into something that fits in your head. That compression is never free. The first rung is the summary statistic, and the book immediately flags that some summaries (QBR, WORP) are opaque while others (yards per catch) are transparent, invoking Moneyball's lesson that batting average hid what on-base percentage revealed. The second rung is the model, and here the book prints real equations rather than hand-waving. Start with ordinary least squares. The linear form y = b0 + b1*x1 + ... + bn*xn is fit by choosing coefficients that minimize the total sum of squared residuals; the footnote explains that squaring keeps residuals positive so the model cannot cheat by underpredicting everything into negative numbers. That is a genuine, dimensionally clean objective, not a toy heuristic. But the book's own touchdown fit exposes the first breakdown: it is a linear probability model, and for mid-field yardlines it returns negative probabilities. A probability cannot be negative, so the linear output map is inadmissible for a chance. The fix is the logistic link, 1/(1+exp(-(b0+...+bn*xn))), which maps the real line into (0,1) by construction. This is the cleanest example in the corpus of a breakdown regime driving a kernel choice: the symptom (negative probabilities) is not patched by clipping but by changing the output map to one whose range is the probability simplex. The same right-hand-side tricks — squares, logs, interactions, fixed effects — survive the switch, because the link only changes how the linear predictor becomes an output. The third rung is interpretation, and the book's best teaching moment is holding things constant. The first_down coefficient on win probability added starts at 0.0573, but first-down plays also gain more yards (15 versus under 4), so part of that coefficient is really the yards, not the new set of downs. Add yards_gained to the model and the first_down coefficient falls to 0.0224 — less than half. That drop is omitted-variable bias made visible, and it is the operational meaning of a partial effect: the coefficient is what remains of a variable's association once the other included variables are held fixed. The crucial caveat, which the book states, is that 'held constant' is a claim about the model's conditioning set, not a certificate of causation; if a confounder is missing, or a control is itself an outcome, the partial effect is still biased. The fourth rung is the composite score, and the book is refreshingly hostile to it. SPARQ and passer rating combine weighting with rescaling: raw components in incompatible units (forty time in seconds, vertical in inches) are first converted to percentiles against a peer group, then weighted into one number. The rescaling is what makes the sum dimensionally legitimate; without it you would be adding seconds to inches. But the author refuses to trust composites because their weights and normalizations are unpublished — 'do you know how to calculate QBR?' — and prefers the component columns. That opacity veto is the through-line of the whole book: a compression you cannot audit is a compression you cannot trust. Read sovereignly, the ladder teaches that each step from data to insight buys convenience with an assumption, and the discipline is to name the assumption, watch for its breakdown symptom, and keep the auditable components rather than the opaque index.

The league-mate who drafts on gut believes the crowd overreacts to injury news and expects to find value the models miss. Recurse: the author knows the gut drafter thinks the market overreacts, so he expects that drafter to reach for 'bounce-back' players; the gut drafter knows the author trusts the efficient-market coefficient, so he expects to be told his pick is already priced.
