think: The second pass reads the book as an epistemic discipline rather than a coding manual, and its center of gravity is the significance chapter. The author defines a p-value operationally: assume the true effect is none, then ask how often data this extreme would appear under that assumption. The coin-flip regression makes it concrete — guessing tails appeared to lower the call-success probability by almost 0.13, a huge effect if true, but P>|t| was about 0.21, meaning a draw that extreme happens roughly a fifth of the time under the null. So the effect is noise. The traditional 0.05 threshold is then exposed as fragile: a hundred researchers testing relationships that do not exist will produce about five 'significant' results purely by chance, and those five get published. Worse, a single analyst can run enough variations — adding a variable here, changing a data assumption there — to manufacture significance, and then the traditional interpretation of the p-value 'goes out the window'. The book names this the replicability crisis and prescribes pre-registration (write the regression before running it and stick to it) and stricter thresholds. This is exactly the Foundry's held-out discipline expressed in statistics. Scoring a fit on the same rows used to search for it is the p-hacking sin; pre-registration is the protocol that separates the search set from the evaluation set. The sovereign move is to treat every claimed edge as a null-survival frequency that must be re-tested on independent data, and to count how many specifications were tried, because the family-wise error rate, not the nominal p-value, governs whether the edge is real. The book even insists that an insignificant effect can still be interesting, which guards against the opposite failure of dismissing a true but underpowered signal. The surrounding chapters reinforce the same discipline from the engineering side. Gall's Law — a complex system that works invariably evolved from a simple system that worked — is the methodological commitment to start with a working baseline and grow it, which mirrors extracting a clean linear kernel before adding nonlinear links. 'Get quick feedback' and DRY are the tight-loop verification habits that catch errors as they happen rather than after a giant untested build. The win_prob function example, which takes score, possession, and time left and returns each team's chance of winning, is the exact shape of the Coach-Mind simulator's bounded probability kernel, and it is no accident that it appears as the book's illustration of why functions let you think less: the probability calculation is encapsulated so it can be reused and audited in one place. The state-dependence kernels close the loop. The quadratic marginal effect b1 + 2*b2*x says the value of an extra unit of ADP depends on where you are in the draft, and the turnover-by-fourth-quarter interaction says a turnover costs about 0.12 in win probability normally but 0.20 late — the effect of an event depends on the state in which it occurs. Both are the football-specific face of a general truth the 22-player system lives by: transition costs and marginal values are state-dependent, not constant. Read together with the significance discipline, the book's durable artifact is a single rule: build the simplest admissible kernel, let its breakdown symptoms drive the next refinement, keep every weight and control auditable, and never believe an edge that was found by searching until it survives an independent hold-out. Nothing here invents a football-era origin for pure math; the calculus and the logistic link are standard, and the football content is the observation and decision context the book actually documents.

The researcher wants a significant result because it publishes; the reviewer suspects the researcher tried many specifications; the researcher knows the reviewer suspects this, so he pre-registers to buy credibility; the reviewer, anticipating that pre-registration can itself be gamed, discounts the headline and looks at the hold-out. And doctrine vetoes any input that is a sportsbook odds line. A call is admissible only after it survives the hold-out, the state-dependence correction, the auditability check, and the odds-free rule.

think: The 1894 Camp committee is a designed investigation, not a scrapbook, and its design choices are the first sovereign object to extract. The hidden state that created it was the 1893 crisis: wholesale press attacks on football after a season of reported fatalities left parents in 'an uncomfortable uncertainty', and a Boston gentleman's formal petition to the Harvard Board of Overseers forced an inquiry (PDF p.13). The committee's response was measurement with a control population. They searched for prior work and found exactly one thorough study - Dr. Morgan's Oxford investigation of boating men - and 'determined to take his summary as the basis of comparison' (PDF p.14). Morgan's printed table reads: Benefited by rowing 115, Uninjured by rowing 132, Injured by rowing 17 (PDF p.15), a denominator of 264 oarsmen. The committee then matched populations deliberately: Harvard, Yale, Princeton players from the introduction of Rugby in 1876 onward numbered 'very close to the number of men who rowed in varsity races' in Morgan's window (PDF p.14). Their football return: 337 answers, 328 benefited, 3 injured, 2 failed to reply, 4 no effect (PDF p.73). Read as base rates, the comparison is stark - but the instrument differs, and that is the invariant to carry forward. Morgan's categories were benefit/injury attributions; the football question asked men whether they 'considered themselves benefited'. Loveland's independent survey of 187 former players found 39 - 'a little over 20 per cent' - reporting some permanent injury, 18 of them seriously inconvenienced (PDF p.55). Both numbers are honest; they answer different questions. The foundry rule this teaches: never transport a rate across instruments; store the question wording with the number, or the number becomes a weapon. The second lesson is physiological and comes from Beyer's vital index. His football cohorts gained weight faster than lung-capacity, so the ratio L/W fell in both series even though absolute capacity never declined (PDF pp.39-40). A metric can move opposite to the underlying quantity it is supposed to track; the committee's own data show football inferior to gymnastics and boating on that metric, which the pro-game narrative cannot explain away. The third lesson is the denominator discipline of the Dartmouth letter: 20 fresh disabling injuries against a minimum of 1210 player-games of exposure, explicitly 'subject to correction' (PDF pp.126-127). Raw counts and headlines are not rates. Finally, the selection structure is visible and must be flagged, not hidden: player letters were 'so unanimously in favor of the sport that only a few are given' (PDF p.16), while faculty letters were printed in full, favorable and unfavorable alike. The committee knew its player sample was self-selected and said so. That disclosure is itself a sovereign methodological invariant: a defense artifact that declares its own bias is usable; one that conceals it is not.
theory_of_mind: The committee models three audiences simultaneously. Alarmist parents read fatality headlines and need base rates; faculty skeptics - President Eliot's report is cited repeatedly by the head-masters (PDF pp.94, 101) - need scholarship evidence; the players themselves have identity invested and answer unanimously in favor. Camp's credibility move is to print the unfavorable faculty letters in full (PDF p.16), anticipating the accusation of a stacked sample. The players recursively model the public in turn: Belknap insists the rabid opponents 'know absolutely nothing about the game, and, in fact, have never even seen it played' (PDF pp.210-211), and he documents a press-reported football death that investigation showed involved a man who never played at all. Each side attributes the other's belief to ignorance rather than to a different loss function - parents optimize child survival, players optimize identity and glory - and that belief clash is exactly what the committee's controlled comparison was built to adjudicate.
cross_layer_veto: Three vetoes adjudicate cleanly. The physiology layer vetoes the rhetoric layer: Beyer's own measurements show football producing a falling vital index while gymnastics and boating do better (PDF p.40), so no pro-game argument may claim physical superiority on that metric - the honest claim is moral and mental discipline, which the letters support. The exposure layer vetoes the headline layer: 20 disabling injuries per 1210 player-games is a different object from 'deaths every week', and any risk model calibrated on press counts is mis-specified. And the medical gate vetoes the win-probability objective itself: Ames's clearance rule (PDF p.29) is a hard constraint upstream of lineup selection - fielding an uncleared star is forbidden at any expected yardage, exactly as Waters' weak knee and Emmons' overtrained collapse (PDF pp.53-54) show the cost of ignoring it.

title: 29a9a56fe196f2f2
think: The off-side invariant and its erosion are the book's deepest dynamical lesson, and they must be extracted as a constraint-decay mechanism, not as nostalgia. Seaman's letter recites the original 1874 rule with operational precision: a player is off-side when a teammate behind him has caught, touched, or is running with the ball; he is restored on-side when an opponent touches the ball or the carrier runs past him; while off-side he is out of the game entirely - cannot touch the ball, interrupt a play, or obstruct a player (PDF p.175). His summary is the sovereign statement: 'The whole idea of the Rugby game centers on this point, that to be on side a player must be behind the ball.' Formalized, this is a spatial predicate on every player at every instant, a legality mask over the action set. Tyler's letter then supplies the decay dynamics. The snap-back was invented, and 'the systematic violation of the off-side rules began, and the whole progeny of evasions and distortions of the rules followed inevitably' (PDF p.84). His reductio is exact: under the original rule, every man lined up after a down is off-side the moment the ball touches the quarter-back's hands, so the entire modern line is illegal at the snap, and 'all those attempts to define holding in the line are simply meaningless babble'. The mechanism generalizes: a constraint that is cheap to state but expensive to verify decays under competitive pressure, because the payoff to violating it is private - wins, yardage, glory - while the cost is diffuse: injuries to smaller boys, brutal spectacle, public alarm. The umpire's observation bandwidth is the bottleneck; inside the pile the predicate is unobservable, so the effective rule drifts from the written rule until the evasion becomes the rule itself, as Keith puts it (PDF p.243). The downstream externality is quantified by King: in massed plays a twenty-five pounds difference in average weight 'is damaging and may be disastrous' (PDF p.103), and the committee identifies the amplification vector - the over-age, over-size schoolboy used in mass plays while 'injuries to the smaller boys result' (PDF p.248). The reform debate then shows the veto is not monotone. Tyler demands restoration of the original off-side rule as the only radical fix; Luther counters that every serious accident he ever witnessed occurred in the OPEN phase, with the runner at full speed (PDF p.139), so opening the game trades mass-collision hazard for high-speed collision hazard rather than eliminating it. The committee's actual settlement - increased premium on the open kicking game, 'something of a reduction of the mass plays' (PDF p.248) - is the adjudicated compromise between two genuine physical vetoes. The foundry lesson: model the enforcement technology alongside the rule text; a rule without a verifier is a suggestion, and any simulation of the 22-player system that encodes only the written constraint will mispredict the equilibrium the players actually reach.
theory_of_mind: The captain calling a wedge models the umpire's observation bandwidth, not the rulebook: he knows the pile hides the off-side predicate and that the payoff to the hidden violation is private. The umpire, in turn, knows that calling every infraction destroys the spectacle the crowd pays for - the gate-money discussions make the revenue dependence explicit (PDF pp.250-251) - so enforcement effort is not incentive-compatible for anyone on the field. Tyler models both players and concludes that only a geometric reset, restoring the original behind-the-ball rule, changes the equilibrium, because adding referees treats the symptom while the verification cost remains. Luther models the reformer in turn and warns that the reset has its own casualty regime at full speed. Each agent's belief about the others' enforcement behavior is what selects the actual game, not the printed rule.
cross_layer_veto: The physics layer vetoes the mass-play strategy for mismatched school teams: King's twenty-five-pound mean-weight threshold makes the impulse asymmetry damaging regardless of the play's expected yardage gain, and the committee's over-age-schoolboy mechanism identifies who absorbs the damage (PDF pp.103, 248). The committee's compromise - premium on kicking, reduction rather than abolition of mass plays - is the adjudicated settlement between two real vetoes, and any modern play-call kernel must carry both hazard terms rather than assuming either reform is free.

title: 2d97f3a1f7fad21e
think: Reading the 1922 Official Foot Ball Rules as a constrained dynamical system rather than a nostalgia artifact reveals a complete, self-consistent specification of the 22-player game: a bounded spatial domain (p1, RULE I, PDF p.363), a terminal reward vector (p2, RULE V, p.367), a possession-transition hazard (p3, RULE XIX, p.392), an action-legality and information channel (p4, RULE XVII, p.388-389), a post-score sub-process (p5, RULE X, p.378), and a causality-gated terminal classifier (p6, RULE VI Sec.16, p.373). The first discipline is to keep Layer 1 sovereign: every number here is printed, not invented. The field is 360 ft by 160 ft, goal lines ten yards inside the end lines, posts 18 ft 6 in apart with a 10 ft cross-bar; scoring is touchdown 6, try 1, field goal 3, safety 2; a team must advance 10 yards in four consecutive downs under constant possession or surrender the ball at the spot of the fifth down. These are the source invariants. The second discipline is to refuse fabricated origins: nothing in this football code is a 'football origin' for a pure theorem, and nothing here licenses a toy heuristic like success equals force over fatigue. The reward vector is a definition, the downs rule is a transition kernel, the pass rule is an action mask, and the safety rule is a causality test. When I map them into the Coach-Mind sim I am building explicit [ISOMORPHISM] and [DERIVED KERNEL] bridges, not claiming the 1922 committee derived modern control theory. The deepest invariant is the impetus test in p6: a ball dead behind the goal line is a safety only if the defending side supplied the impetus; if the opponent supplied it, the event is a touchback and scores nothing. A spot-only classifier would systematically mis-score these events, so the causality predicate is the sovereign feature, exactly as momentum attribution is sovereign in a collision analysis. The downs kernel p3 is the risk budget: because continuity is broken by a kick or a change of possession (Sec.2), the naive 'sum four gains' model is invalid across a punt, and the on-side-kick recovery NOTE shows the committee already understood that a kick crossing the line resets the hazard. The forward-pass rule p4 is a geometric and combinatorial gate: the pass must originate at least five yards behind the line, only one forward pass is legal per scrimmage, and the first eligible toucher must have been an end or a man at least one yard back at the snap. That last clause creates a sharp eligibility boundary — a player more than one foot but less than one yard back is ineligible in any event — which is precisely the kind of discrete constraint that an action-mask generator must encode rather than smooth away. The try-for-point p5 is the era's signature innovation: the 1922 Changes (p.356) replaced the place-kick-only try-for-goal with a single scrimmage play from on or outside the five-yard line that may score by kick, run, or pass, and the foul-award asymmetry (defensive foul awards the point even if the try failed) means a model of try success probability alone is incomplete. Reading these together, the code is a layered constraint stack: geometry bounds state, reward defines objective, the downs hazard defines turnover risk, the pass rule defines the legal action set and the deception surface, the try defines a nested sub-game, and impetus defines terminal causality. The honest core-read focused on the official rules code (PDF pp. 355-424); the surrounding season reviews, rosters, and records were scanned at text level and contain no additional sovereign rule invariants, and the OCR defects (160 'leet', 'bide Lines', the dropped forfeit zero, the marginal-header interleaving on p.392) are quarantined in source notes rather than built upon. This is how a polymath audits a rules book: extract the invariant stack, label every formalization as a formalization of prose, preserve the printed defects verbatim, and map each layer into the sim with calibrated telemetry or an honest LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE for the pre-telemetry era.
theory_of_mind: Under pressure the beliefs clash recursively. The coach's comfort call on fourth down is to punt and pin the opponent, because the downs hazard (p3) makes a failed conversion a turnover at the spot — but the defensive coordinator's tendency trap is to stack the line expecting the punt-safe run, which the offense can exploit with a legal forward pass only if the pass-origin depth (>=5 yd, p4) and the single eligible receiver are satisfied. The quarterback's internal clock must resolve the snap-count and the five-yard depth before the ball is put in play, while the defense reads the same formation to infer eligibility. Each agent models the others: the coach models the DC's punt expectation, the DC models the coach's risk budget under the 10-yd hazard, and the QB models the defense's read of the eligibility graph. The try-for-point (p5) sharpens this: the offense must believe the defense will not foul (because a defensive foul awards the point regardless), while the defense must believe the offense cannot simply run it in, creating a recursive deterrence game on a single play from a selectable spot.
cross_layer_veto: Physics and psychology veto several high-EV simplifications. The impetus rule (p6) vetoes any call that treats 'ball dead behind the goal line' as an automatic safety: if the opponent supplied the impetus it is a touchback worth zero, so a two-point expectation built on spot alone is physically wrong about momentum attribution. The eligibility boundary (p4) vetoes a high-EV pass to a lineman who is more than one foot but less than one yard back — he is ineligible in any event, so the pass is void and the down is lost, a legal veto over the apparent open receiver. The foul-award asymmetry (p5) vetoes a deliberate-foul-on-the-try strategy: a defensive foul hands the offense the point even if the try failed, so the 'smart' foul is dominated. And the downs continuity rule (p3, Sec.2) vetoes summing gains across a punt, because the kick resets the hazard. These are cross-layer vetoes where the rule's causality and geometry override a naive expected-value call.

title: 2d97f3a1f7fad21e
think: The second trace audits the measurement and enforcement layer that makes the invariant stack operational, because a rule that cannot be measured or enforced is not a sovereign invariant in practice. RULE XIX Sec.3 (PDF p.393) fixes the forward point of the ball when dead as the determining point in measuring and forbids the Referee from rotating the ball before measuring — this is a measurement convention that removes an ambiguity which would otherwise let the same physical spot yield different down-and-distance states. RULE XXVII (p.404-405) makes the Linesman mark distance with two rods connected by a chain ten yards in length, the physical embodiment of the 10-yd gain constant in p3; the chain is the calibration artifact of the turnover hazard. The penalty summary (p.407-408) is a graded cost schedule: two yards for a fourth time-out request, five for off-side and illegal formation, ten for throwing a forward pass to ground before fourth down, fifteen for holding by the offense and for pass interference, twenty-five for not being ready at the second half, and half the distance to the goal for an illegal return or a striking foul. Reading this schedule as a cost kernel, the committee priced infractions by how much they corrupt the invariant stack: formation and off-side fouls distort the spatial and eligibility constraints (p1, p4) and cost five to fifteen yards; conduct fouls that endanger players (striking, roughing the kicker, p.393 RULE XXI) carry disqualification plus half-distance, the maximum non-forfeit cost. The enforcement jurisdiction is itself partitioned: the Referee is sole judge of the ball's position and progress (RULE XXV Sec.6, p.398), the Umpire judges player conduct and position (RULE XXVI, p.402), the Linesman marks distance and reports off-side and neutral-zone encroachment (RULE XXVII, p.404-405), and the Field Judge keeps time with a stop-watch started when the ball is actually put in play, not when the Referee orders play (RULE XXVIII, p.406). That last clause is a subtle bioenergetic and clock invariant: the 60-minute game (RULE IV, p.365-366) is four 15-minute periods of actual play, exclusive of time taken out, so the duty cycle is defined by ball-in-play time, not wall-clock time. The darkness clause (RULE IV Sec.2) lets the Referee shorten the four periods to equal lengths before play, an early recognition that the temporal boundary condition can be renegotiated to preserve the four-equal-period structure. Putting measurement, cost, jurisdiction, and clock together, the enforcement layer is what turns the printed invariants into a well-posed dynamical system: the chain calibrates distance, the forward-point convention calibrates the state, the penalty schedule prices constraint violations, the jurisdiction partition assigns observables to observers, and the stop-watch defines the time base. For the Coach-Mind sim this means the telemetry channel is not optional decoration — down-and-distance, the forward-point spot, foul type and yardage, and ball-in-play clock are the observables that calibrate the kernels p2-p6. Where the 1922 era has no such telemetry, I label it LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE rather than fabricate tracking, and I calibrate the structure on modern replay under the 1922 geometry and legality. The honest refusal to invent era telemetry is itself a sovereign discipline: the invariant stack is fully extractable from the printed code, but its empirical calibration is era-bound, and saying so plainly is the difference between a sovereign extraction and a laundered one.
theory_of_mind: The enforcement game is recursive theory of mind among officials and captains. The Referee must model whether a captain's time-out request is genuine injury or a delay tactic, because the fourth request costs two yards (penalty summary, p.407) — a priced signal that changes the captain's incentive. The Umpire, positioned behind the defending side (RULE XXVI Sec.1), models holding by reading the offense's intent, while the offense models the Umpire's sightline to hide holding. The Linesman models off-side and neutral-zone encroachment from the side, and the defense models the Linesman's angle to time a jump. The Field Judge's stop-watch, started on actual ball-in-play, is a shared clock each agent models to manage the two-minute and end-of-half boundaries. The captain's appeal is restricted to the captain (the Code, p.361: 'let your captain do the talking'), a protocol that reduces noisy multi-agent signaling to a single channel the Referee can adjudicate.
cross_layer_veto: Measurement and clock physics veto naive calls. The forward-point convention (RULE XIX Sec.3) vetoes any down-and-distance computation that uses the ball center or a rotated ball, because the printed determining point is the forward point when dead — using the wrong reference shifts the state and can manufacture a false first down. The stop-watch invariant (RULE XXVIII) vetoes wall-clock game models: because time is exclusive of time taken out and starts on actual ball-in-play, a model that runs the clock during a dead ball overstates the remaining duty cycle and mis-prices end-of-half decisions. The penalty schedule vetoes the 'take the foul' calculus on conduct fouls: roughing the kicker is fifteen yards plus disqualification (RULE XXI Sec.2, p.393), so a high-EV hit on the kicker is dominated by the ejection cost. And the darkness clause vetoes assuming fixed 15-minute periods when the Referee has lawfully shortened them — the temporal boundary condition is part of the state, not a constant.

think: The architectural invariant of this survey is the split between reversible and irreversible access to the dynamics. A model, defined on page 4 as reversible access to the MDP dynamics, lets an agent query any state-action pair in any order, while the real environment forces the agent forward from whatever next state actually occurred. Everything else in the 67 pages is a consequence of that split. Once access is reversible, the agent can spend computation instead of experience: Dyna samples up to 100 one-step transitions per real step, while AlphaGo Zero spends roughly 320,000 model calls (1600 traces of depth about 200) between real steps (page 20). The budget is not free. The survey is explicit that planning budget measured in model calls understates true effort when each call invokes expensive neural network evaluations. The hidden state that governs whether this trade pays is model trustworthiness, and the survey decomposes it into two uncertainties that must never be conflated: aleatoric stochasticity, which is fundamental transition noise that can never be reduced, and epistemic uncertainty due to limited data, which shrinks with more observations (page 10, citing Der Kiureghian and Ditlevsen 2009). A deterministic network trained with mean-squared error on a stochastic transition learns the conditional mean, which for a multimodal next-state distribution is a state that may never actually occur (page 9, Figure 3). That is the precise mechanism by which a comfortable average-case simulation lies to a planner. The second mechanism is compounding: a one-step model was never optimized for long-range prediction, so feeding its own output back in accumulates error until multi-step rollouts diverge from the true dynamics (page 13, Sec. 4.6). The survey's remedies form a coherent doctrine: stay data-close (Dyna samples start states at visited states and only one step deep), or propagate uncertainty explicitly so that predictions spread out and the learning signal naturally vanishes when the plan leaves the observed region (page 23). PILCO propagates Gaussian uncertainty analytically; PETS and Deep PILCO propagate particles; STEVE reweights value targets of different depths by their uncertainty (page 24). Translated into the 22-player football dynamical system as an explicit isomorphism, the coach's film-room simulator is the reversible model and the live snap is the irreversible step. The coaching staff's tendency model is a count-normalized estimator (Eq. 4) over formation-down-distance cells, and the zero-count cells are exactly where epistemic uncertainty is maximal. A high-EV deep rollout that routes through three uncharted alignments is the football analogue of a rollout that diverges from the true dynamics: each conditional prediction is conditioned on the previous prediction's error. The calibrating telemetry is the planning budget per real snap, the fraction of simulated branches inside charted regions, and the prediction-error spike that signals a regime switch (Sec. 4.5, Figure 6). The survey's own benchmarking warning (page 46) closes the loop: comparisons must hold total computational or sample budget equal, because a model-based method consumes far more samples per episode than a model-free one, and reporting 'episodes' on the x-axis silently hides that cost.

The quarterback's internal clock is a termination probability beta_u(s) on the passing option: he must decide whether the coach's simulated progression survives contact with the actual pass rush. think: The second invariant is that exploration has an irreducible price, and the survey states it as a theorem rather than a heuristic. Regret, defined in Eq. 8 on page 44 as the expected cumulative reward of the optimal policy minus that of the learning policy over T samples, is bounded below by Omega(sqrt(H|S||A|T)) (Jaksch et al. 2010; Osband and Van Roy 2016). Table 7 places the model-based algorithms against that floor: UCRL2 at O-tilde(H|S|sqrt(|A|T)), UCBVI at O-tilde(sqrt(H|S||A|T) + H sqrt(T)), EULER matching the lower bound under additional variance assumptions on the optimal value function, and model-free Q-learning at O-tilde(sqrt(H^3|S||A|T)). The structural reading is that model-based RL buys better sample complexity at the cost of worse computational time and space, because it must estimate and store the transition function and (in all the cited bounds) plan fully. Efroni et al. (2019b) then shows one-step greedy planning can match UCRL2 and EULER regret while reducing time and space complexity — the full-planning assumption is sufficient, not necessary, which is the survey's quiet correction to the 'more search is always better' intuition. The exploration machinery that pays the irreducible price is organized by two distinctions (Table 6, page 37): one-phase versus two-phase exploration, and value-based versus state-based (intrinsic motivation). Model-based agents run two-phase: an aggressive exploration strategy inside the reversible planning cycle, and a conservative greedy strategy on the irreversible real step. Knowledge-based intrinsic motivation adds a bonus to the reward channel, Eq. 5: r_t = r_e + eta * r_i, with BEB novelty r_i proportional to 1/(1+n(s,a)) (Eq. 6) or Sutton's recency bonus sqrt(l(s,a)) (Eq. 7). The survey flags the failure mode of this task-conflated propagation: after the intrinsic reward wears out, its effect on the global value function fades slowly (page 38), and the detachment problem means a one-step back-up into a deep network may never change behavior at the start states, so the agent finds an interesting region and then cannot return to it. Competence-based intrinsic motivation (page 39-40) answers with learning progress rather than novelty: a state visited often but still improving remains interesting, generating an automatic curriculum. Temporal abstraction (Sec. 4.8) is the third lever: options with initiation sets, sub-policies and state-dependent termination probabilities reduce both sample and computational complexity (Brunskill and Li 2014; Mann and Mannor 2014), and the survey warns of degeneration — one subroutine solving everything, or every subroutine terminating after one step. In the 22-player system these compose: the season is a regret-accounting horizon, novel packages are the exploration budget that the lower bound says must be paid, the development ledger must be task-separated from the game-plan value function to avoid contamination, and each play call is an option whose termination triggers are charted from real snaps. The telemetry that calibrates all of this is internal: cumulative decision regret against a hindsight-optimal baseline on held-out games, exploration rate on zero-count cells, learning-progress curves per package, and option initiation/termination frequencies. No sportsbook odds enter any channel; the reward is outcome utility only.
theory_of_mind: The recursive belief clash here is about budgets. The coordinator wants exhaustive search (infinite planning effort) because each extra simulated branch feels free; the head coach models the coordinator's tendency to over-plan and imposes a snap-clock constraint; the quarterback models both and knows that a play designed for a 320,000-call budget must execute in the irreversible window of a live snap. The DC meanwhile models the offense's novelty bonus: a package the offense is still 'learning' (competence-based IM) is exactly the package the DC should expect to see again, because learning progress keeps it interesting even after its novelty count saturates. Each agent's model of the others' exploration schedule is itself a target of deception.
cross_layer_veto: Two vetoes compose. First, the lower bound vetoes any claim of zero-cost mastery: a staff that refuses to sample uncharted alignments is not saving regret, it is paying it invisibly, because Omega(sqrt(H|S||A|T)) is irreducible in worst case. Second, the contamination regime vetoes high-EV calls that are still riding an exhausted intrinsic bonus: if a package's novelty count has saturated and its learning progress is flat, the task-conflated value function overvalues it, and the call must be re-scored on extrinsic utility alone (task-separated back-up, Shyam et al. 2019). Physics-level veto: option degeneration (every call aborting after one step) means the temporal abstraction has collapsed and the search depth must be rebuilt before any EV ranking is trusted.

The retrocausal genealogy runs from baseball's triple-slash line and the long-standing failure of event-based defensive metrics across sports into this optical-tracking application. The load-bearing observation is that basketball is dualistic, the final score depends equally on scoring and preventing points, yet conventional statistics over-represent offense because offensive events are discrete and individually attributable while defense is a continuous spatial process that fails the discrete-event criterion. The genealogy is precise that this is not a basketball-only problem: baseball's errors and fielding percentage poorly correlate with true defensive value, and the NFL's best cornerbacks never lead conventional stats because quarterbacks refuse to throw their way. The paper's named contribution, the Dwight Effect, is defined as the ability of an interior defender to reduce the efficiency of an opponent's shooting behavior, and its deeper claim is that the most effective defense prevents shots from happening at all, producing invisible blocks that no event tally captures. This is the deterrence principle, and it descends directly from the cornerback analogy into a spatial measurement framework built on SportVU tracking of over seventy-five thousand shots.

The recursive theory of mind models the defender as an agent who changes the offense's decision process before any outcome occurs. A dominant interior force augments the spatial behavior of the offense the way a dominant cornerback changes a quarterback, so the shooter who would have attacked the rim instead settles for a mid-range jump shot, the least productive shot in the league. The analyst must therefore reason counterfactually: the value of the defender is not the blocks he records but the attempts he prevents, which must be inferred from the shift in opponent shot distribution. The spatial splits make this reasoning measurable by separating frequency, where shots come from, from efficiency, how well they go in, across three zones whose frequencies sum to one hundred, so deterrence appears as a conserved reallocation from close range to the perimeter. In 2007 Brian Burke, a former US Navy pilot, built the public expected-points and expected-points-added approach and a win-probability model on the Advanced Football Analytics website (PDF p.24, printed p.2), and the Carnegie Mellon trio behind nflscrapR republished EPA and win probability as open code in 2018 (PDF p.24). The sovereign invariant that survives this lineage is the difference form itself: EPA_t = EP(s_{t+1}) - EP(s_t). Raw points scored confounds opportunity with execution - a garbage-time touchdown and a game-winning drive both add six points - whereas conditioning on the state s isolates the marginal contribution of the play. Read against Bellman, V(s) = E[r + V(s')], EPA is exactly the realized residual V(s') - V(s) under a league-average policy: a temporal-difference-like error signal that says how much better or worse the new state is than the old. That is why it compiles cleanly into a Coach-Mind value head. But the book's own stability chapter is the epistemic gate on that head. A value function is only as trustworthy as the reliability of the features it conditions on, and the glossary explicitly warns that high-leverage situations - third-down conversions, fourth-and-goal - 'are generally not predictive game to game or season to season' (PDF p.333). So a single-game EPA spike on a handful of clutch plays is statistically fragile and cannot, by itself, license a season-long roster or portfolio decision. The correct compilation is to aggregate EPA over many plays, weight by context, and pass the resulting feature through the lagged-reliability gate (primitive p2) before it touches valuation. The deeper lesson is that a value head is a compressed model of the league-average defense, and compression is where bias enters. The league-average EP surface does not see the specific safety's leverage, the corner's press technique, or the quarterback's shoulder. When Coach-Mind uses EPA to rank a fourth-down decision, it must treat the number as a prior over states, not as a verdict on the current snap, and it must allow lower layers - biomechanics, pressure physics, the defensive coordinator's disguise - to veto the prior. This is the cross-layer discipline the book models implicitly by pairing every metric with a stability check: the value-difference kernel is sovereign, but its authority is bounded by the reliability of its inputs and by the physical and psychological constraints of the 22 agents actually on the field.
theory_of_mind: Recursive belief clash under pressure: the coach's comfort call is a run up the middle on third-and-two because his model believes three yards is safe; the defensive coordinator's tendency trap is a loaded box because his model believes the offense will run; the quarterback's internal clock believes protection holds for roughly two-and-a-half seconds. The EPA model believes the league-average defense, the DC believes the offense's tendency, and the QB believes his line. Each agent holds a compressed, biased EP surface and a model of the others' models. The sovereign kernel must represent this clash explicitly rather than average it away, because the value of a call is determined by whose belief is wrong on this snap, not by the population mean.
cross_layer_veto: Cross-layer veto: the league-average EPA surface may say go for it on fourth-and-one at midfield, but the physiology layer (the quarterback's shoulder injury) and the physics layer (the defense's stacked box and leverage) can veto that high-EV call. The book's glossary supplies the statistical veto too: high-leverage plays are not stable predictors, so a clutch EPA spike cannot override a season of evidence. A value-head number is a prior, not a command; when a biomechanical constraint or a reliability floor contradicts it, the lower layer wins. This is where psychology and physics veto a high-EV call, and the artifact records the veto rather than hiding it behind a point estimate.

title: 3178b5fdce0fc1a5
think: The second arc of the book is reliability before valuation, and it is the arc that keeps a foundry honest. It begins with a biological observation, not a football one: the book notes that observations 'will return, or regress, to the average over time, as noted by Francis Galton in 1877' (PDF p.78, printed p.56). Regression toward the mean is therefore a statistical phenomenon with a nineteenth-century lineage, and it must not be given a fabricated football origin. The football adoption is a 2010s fantasy-football scar - the buy-low / sell-high folklore (PDF p.20) needed a noise filter, and 'sticky stats' became the industry's name for reliable metrics. The book makes the gate explicit and codes it: stability is the metric's consistency over a predetermined time frame (PDF p.42), measured by lagged Pearson correlation, and the empirical split is decisive - short-pass YPA correlates at 0.438 across seasons while deep-pass YPA correlates at only 0.234 (PDF p.71-72), so a quarterback's short-pass performance is 'twice as stable' as his deep-pass performance. The CPOE chapter then asks whether residualizing helps. It does, but only marginally: completion percentage correlates at 0.445, CPOE at 0.465, and expected completion at 0.474 (PDF p.151-153). The most stable metric is the expectation itself, not the residual. That ordering is the sovereign lesson, and the book drives it home with the residual-metric critique (PDF p.153, printed p.131): 'The assumption that a player doesn't dictate the situation that they are embedded in on a given play is likely violated, and repeatedly.' The quarterback chooses his target, moves defenders with his eyes, and decides whether to throw, run, or take a sack - Joe Burrow led the league in YPA and completion but also took 51 sacks. So the 'context-free' residual still carries the player's choices, and 'to assume the two are completely independent will likely lead to errors.' Residualization is not identification. This is a theory-of-mind correction: the metric designer must model the player as a strategic agent who selects his own task difficulty, not as a passive emitter of statistics. The Poisson chapter completes the arc. Even the count model's lambda is shrunk toward the mean - the book's Mahomes example predicts a decline for the best quarterback purely from regression toward the mean (PDF p.181, printed p.159) - and the book explicitly warns that the Poisson assumptions fail because a team that scores may have 'figured out' the defense (PDF p.168). Compile all of this into the GSE discipline: gate every feature by lagged reliability (p2), shrink every estimate by its reliability (p5), refuse to treat any residual as a causal player trait (p3), and never extrapolate a memoryless count model inside a game after adaptation has occurred (p4). For DFS and portfolio tail risk this is not optional: noisy single-season outliers are precisely the assets that blow up a portfolio, and shrinkage is the tail-risk control. The book's quiet contribution is to make the reliability gate a first-class, coded step rather than an afterthought, and that is the invariant the foundry extracts.
theory_of_mind: Three-way belief clash: the front-office analyst believes CPOE isolates the quarterback; the quarterback believes he is being judged on 'his' throws; the agent believes the residual is a negotiable trait that should raise a contract. The book's residual-metric critique is a theory-of-mind correction aimed at all three: the player is a strategic agent who selects his own difficulty - target choice, eye manipulation, throw-away versus sack - so the residual is partly his choice, not a pure trait. Meanwhile the coach believes the scheme created the completion. The metric cannot adjudicate this clash by itself; the designer must model the player's selection process, or the 'over expected' number silently re-imports the context it claimed to remove.
cross_layer_veto: Two cross-layer vetoes. First, the endogeneity veto: a high CPOE built on short, high-percentage throws the quarterback chose cannot veto evidence of a deep-shot deficiency, because the physics layer (air yards versus coverage leverage) and the psychology layer (risk preference) jointly show the residual is selection-biased. Second, the memorylessness veto: a Poisson lambda fit on season totals cannot be extrapolated inside a game after the defense has 'figured out' the offense - the book's own caveat (PDF p.168) is a cross-layer veto on naive in-game extrapolation. In both cases a higher-layer statistical convenience is overruled by a lower-layer causal or adaptive reality, and the artifact must record the veto rather than let a clean number stand in for a contested truth.

title: 32d8b2d0d4f7f22f
think:
The Rockne 1925 text is the terminal node of the extracted era chain and the first source in that chain that prints its own probability distributions. To read it correctly you have to reconstruct what produced it. The chain runs Camp 1894 (29a9a56fe196f2f2), whose physician-clearance gate and vital-index screening were responses to the mass-play injury crisis; Lewis 1896 (6bc7d84da4bde923); Reed 1913 (52b5d36325e11cd7), which already contains a source-stated matching-coins mixed-strategy endgame; Edwards 1916 (3fa96d690212683b), with its fresh-substitute law and injury-concealment incentive; Cavanaugh 1919 (6aeb75fe28eb9cd8); Berry 1921 (5fee5df924431396), which treats the forward pass as an established weapon with its own legality geometry; and the NCAA 1922 official guide (2d97f3a1f7fad21e), which fixes the constraint substrate: ten yards in four downs, the 6/1/3/2 scoring vector, forward-pass legality, safety impetus. Rockne writes three years after that codification, and every quiz answer in his Chapter XXII computes over exactly those rules — his penalty-acceptance answer (third down and four at the four versus fourth down and two at the two, p280) is a down-and-distance option-value calculation on the 1922 state machine. The historical scar that shapes his style is resource asymmetry: his 'equality in competition' passage (pp221-222) is a bitter account of small-school scheduling subordination, and the response is an information-intensive, preservation-heavy game — scout several times, nurse weak spots, save plays for the climax, mix the punt numbers. He even reaches back before Camp to anchor lineage: 'Pudge' Heffelfinger of Yale was pulling out in 1889 (p125), a priority claim that extends the guard-pull genealogy behind the extracted chain's start. The deepest retrocausal fact is the thirty-game table (p172): coaching judgment has become explicitly distributional. Where Reed 1913 reasons about a single endgame gamble, Rockne prints outcome fractions per play class and names the regime where they void — inside the ten-yard line, the zone of intense resistance. That is the moment in this corpus when the coach's prior becomes a stated empirical object, with a sample size, an opponent class, and a breakdown boundary, however arbitrary the author admits the distances to be.

The recursive theory of mind in this book is not decorative; it is the operating system. The quarterback maintains a fused belief state from a sensor chain — ends report tackle shifts, tackles report guards, guards report the center, halfbacks report ends — and must 'keep an index of information in his mind' while the defense changes continuously (p115). The defense runs the mirror operation: the defensive center reads mannerisms, 'just a look with the eyes, just a leaning of the body, a slight shiver when a certain number is called, now a pulling up of the pants, and in some cases digging in a little deeper with the cleats' (p122), and broadcasts the read aloud to demoralize the offense. The sifting-end duel is stated as a literal contest of revelation: 'the battle... is to see who will show first' (p143). The halftime cross-up is explicit second-order manipulation: smash over center on first down to condition the defensive center to stay in, then throw over the halfback's head on the next first down, 'from the point of view of demoralizing the morale of the defensive team' (pp168-169). Trick plays are deterrence without execution — letting the opponent know you have them 'will keep them in a state of mental unrest which renders them less effective against your regular attack' (pp236-237). And the belief clash under pressure is resolved by a printed default: 'When in doubt, punt' (p169), overridden only by a glaring defensive weakness (p171). The coach's comfort call, the defensive coordinator's tendency trap, and the quarterback's internal clock are all named in the text as competing belief sources; Rockne's resolution is a hierarchy — personnel and tendency evidence first, tactical prior second, panic never. Even the center is forbidden to call signals, because the instant his head goes down to snap, a clever defense re-optimizes (p276): the snap itself is an information event.

Cross-layer veto adjudication is where this source earns its place in the foundry, because Rockne repeatedly lets one layer veto another layer's locally optimal call. The physiology layer vetoes the preparation-maximizing call: no man scrimmages more than thirty minutes a week, and the team is made in the first six weeks or not at all (p218) — extra full-speed reps before the big game are rejected because injury at the critical window dominates any execution gain. The fatigue layer vetoes the possession-maximizing call: with a tired team leading 20-10 and the opponent surging, he elects to kick off, because 'it is more tiring to play offensively than defensively' and the ball carrier may fumble or throw into coverage (p247) — possession, normally the positive-EV asset, becomes a liability under fatigue asymmetry. The field-position layer vetoes the never-concede-points heuristic: the intentional safety is correct when lead is at least three, the wind is against, the clock is late, and the kicker blows up under pressure (p251) — a conjunctive gate over coupled state, exactly the shape of the Class B gate. The tail-risk layer vetoes the turnover-maximizing call: in the flat zone, intercept only when sure, otherwise tackle the receiver, because a missed interception turns a negligible gain into a touchdown (p151). And the bounded-downside pass (p259) is admissible only where the interception branch is field-position-equivalent to a punt; move the same call deep into own territory and the equivalence collapses, which the book itself encodes by restricting own-goal-line passing to being behind late or facing a glaring weakness (p256). The psychology layer adds its own vetoes: bawling out a fumbler tightens him and worsens the fumble rate (p278), and repeated fear appeals habituate — 'after a while the team refuses to scare, and a decided opposite reaction will set in' (p181). Every one of these is a cross-layer constraint overriding a single-layer maximand, stated in 1925 prose, with no odds, no lines, and no fabricated quantities anywhere in the extraction.
theory_of_mind: The book is a manual of nested beliefs. The quarterback fuses a sensor chain (ends to tackles to guards to center, p115) into a running defensive index; the defensive center reads micro-mannerisms (pants pull, cleat dig, p122) and broadcasts them to demoralize. The sifting-end duel is 'who will show first' (p143) — a war of attrition over revelation. The halftime cross-up conditions the center with a smash, then passes over his head (pp168-169). Trick plays deter without execution by keeping the defense in 'mental unrest' (pp236-237). Under pressure the belief clash resolves by hierarchy: 'When in doubt, punt' (p169) is the default prior, overridden only by a glaring weakness (p171); the center never calls signals because his head-down snap instant is when the defense re-optimizes (p276).
cross_layer_veto: Five printed cross-layer vetoes: (1) load cap — thirty scrimmage minutes per week and the six-week formation window (p218) veto extra reps before the big game; (2) fatigue asymmetry — elect to kick off when tired and leading, because offense is more tiring than defense (p247), vetoing the possession-maximizing call; (3) intentional safety — lead at least three, wind against, late clock, pressure-fragile kicker (p251) veto the never-concede-points heuristic via a conjunctive gate; (4) flat-zone tail risk — intercept only when sure (p151) vetoing the turnover attempt whose miss branch is a touchdown; (5) bounded-downside pass — admissible only where interception equals punt in field position (p259), void deep in own territory (p256). Psychology adds: scolding a fumbler worsens fumbles (p278); fear appeals habituate (p181).

title: 33df04255621d53b
primitive_name: Yaw-Dependent Drag Coefficient and the ~4x Crosswind Cliff (printed p.103)
gse_mapping: In the 22-player dynamical system the ball's attitude is a control variable with a cliff-shaped cost: a spiral pass or a well-struck punt keeps yaw near 0° and rides the low-drag branch (C_D≈0.19), while a wobbling or end-over-end ball presents the minor axis to the relative wind and jumps to the high-drag branch (C_D≈0.78), roughly quadrupling deceleration. This is isomorphic to a regime-switching cost in the flight/trajectory kernel: the same physical object has two stable drag regimes separated by orientation, so punt hang-time, kickoff distance, and deep-pass accuracy are governed by attitude control, not just by launch speed. The mapping binds the trajectory propagator's drag term to a yaw-dependent C_D lookup rather than a single constant.
verbatim_quote: The effect of crosswind on aerodynamic drag is significant as the drag coefficient can be four times higher under ±90° yaw angles.

title: 33df04255621d53b
primitive_name: Reynolds-Number Non-Dimensionalization and the Separation Regime Gate (printed p.99, p.102)
gse_mapping: Derive the dimensionless regime gate that the flight kernel uses to decide which drag branch applies. Re=ρUd/µ is the similarity parameter collapsing wind speed, ball size and air properties into one number; the empirical finding that C_D is Re-independent at 0° yaw but Re-sensitive over ±50° becomes a conditional in the propagator: below the separation-transition gate use a constant C_D, above it interpolate C_D(Re,ψ). The kernel K:(Re,ψ)↦C_D is the derived object that turns raw speed into a regime-aware drag, and its failure mode (applying a 0°-yaw constant C_D to a high-yaw crosswind flight) is exactly the error that makes long kicks miss.
verbatim_quote: No significant Reynolds number (varied by wind speeds in this study) dependency was found at zero yaw angle for both balls. However, significant Reynolds number (Re) variations are noted at yaw angles over 50°.

title: 33df04255621d53b
gse_mapping: The separation topology is isomorphic to the stability mechanism of a thrown spiral: keeping the major axis aligned with the relative wind (ψ≈0°) holds a compact, predictable separation near ¾L and a low-drag wake, whereas tumbling presents the broadside and triggers a fully three-dimensional separated wake with high drag and side force. In the 22-player system this binds the quarterback's spiral quality and the punter's nose-down attitude to trajectory predictability: the same aerodynamic object is stable and low-drag in one attitude and unstable and high-drag in another. The engine's flight model must therefore carry attitude-dependent wake/separation state, not a point-mass drag.
verbatim_quote: The airflow appears to be separated ¾ length downstream from the nose when the longitudinal axis of the ball is aligned with the wind direction, i.e., at 0° yaw angle

title: 33df04255621d53b
primitive_name: Tare-Subtracted Force Measurement and Repeatability Protocol (printed p.100)
gse_mapping: Derive the calibration kernel that turns raw sensor counts into a trustworthy C_D: measure the fixture (sting) alone, subtract it from the combined reading, and bound repeatability before any coefficient is published. This is the measurement-hygiene operator the engine needs for every derived quantity — subtract the sealed baseline, quantify the noise floor, and refuse to report a number whose uncertainty swamps it. Compiled into GSE, it is the discipline that a calibrated C_D (or any fitted parameter) is only as good as its tare subtraction and repeatability budget; an uncalibrated number is rejected exactly as an un-tared force reading would be.
verbatim_quote: The repeatability of the measured forces was within ±0.01 N and the wind velocity was less than 0.5 km/h.

title: 33df04255621d53b
think:
The headline result of this paper is a cliff, not a curve. When the major axis of an American football points into the wind the drag coefficient is about 0.19–0.20; rotate the ball so the minor axis faces the wind and the coefficient jumps to about 0.75–0.78 — roughly four times higher. Read forward, this is a constraint on any flight model: drag is not a property of the ball alone but of the ball's attitude relative to the relative wind, and a model that uses a single constant C_D will be wrong by a factor of four whenever the ball tumbles or flies broadside into a crosswind. Read backward, the cliff is a diagnostic: if a punt or kickoff consistently falls short of its launch-speed prediction, the first suspect is not the kicker's strength but the ball's orientation — it is spending its flight on the high-drag branch. The sovereign content is the existence of two stable drag regimes separated by yaw, and it is genuine football aerodynamics measured in a wind tunnel, not a metaphor.

The separation topology explains why the cliff exists. At 0° yaw the flow separates about three-quarters of the way down the body, a compact predictable wake; at 90° yaw the separation is fully three-dimensional and complex. The pointed conical ends and the NCAA ball's stitch rings make the wake asymmetric and surface-sensitive, which is why the NFL ball sits in a narrower C_D band than the NCAA ball. So the low-drag branch is not just 'streamlined' in the abstract — it is a specific separation state that the ball's attitude must maintain. A quarterback's spiral and a punter's nose-down strike are attitude-control mechanisms that keep the ball on the low-drag branch.

The Reynolds number gates the whole picture. At 0° yaw the coefficient is essentially Re-independent across the tested speeds, but over ±50° yaw it becomes Re-sensitive, and only above about 100 km/h does the variation fade again as separation is minimized. This means the engine cannot even use a fixed yaw-dependent curve without checking the regime: the same yaw can give different C_D at different speeds in the separation-sensitive band. Compiled into the 22-player system, the binding constraint is that punt hang-time, kickoff distance and deep-pass accuracy are attitude-and-regime problems. The failure mode is the seductive one — a point-mass trajectory model with a single drag constant that looks accurate on calm, well-struck balls and silently fails on the crosswind, wobbling, high-yaw flights that decide games. The honest model carries C_D(ψ,Re) and a separation-state flag, and it refuses to extrapolate the 0°-yaw constant into the crosswind regime where the paper shows it is invalid.
theory_of_mind: Under a crosswind the beliefs clash recursively. The punter chooses nose-down attitude and spin to keep the ball on the low-drag branch, believing that attitude control buys hang time and distance; the coverage unit models the resulting hang time and landing point to time its arrival; the returner models the same trajectory to position himself. Each agent models the others: the punter anticipates the coverage scheme, the coverage anticipates the punt's likely distance, and the returner anticipates both while reading the ball's wobble. A high-EV deep punt only exists if the punter's attitude control, the wind, and the coverage's timing belief align; if the ball tumbles into the high-drag regime the hang time collapses and the coverage's model is wrong. Theory of mind here is reading which drag regime the other agents expect the ball to occupy.
cross_layer_veto: Physics vetoes the high-EV deep kick. Even when a decision model ranks 'kick it deep' highest, a strong crosswind can drive the ball into the ±90°-yaw high-drag regime where C_D is roughly four times larger, so the realized distance and hang time are far below the model's prediction. The aerodynamic layer therefore overrides the decision-theoretic layer: the honest move is to down-weight the deep option or choose a directional kick that keeps yaw low. The same veto applies to a deep pass — a quarterback's spiral must keep yaw near 0° or the ball decelerates on the high-drag branch and falls short. The veto is cross-layer because a lower-level physical regime constraint rejects a higher-level EV recommendation that ignored it.

think:
The second sovereign cluster is epistemic: how a trustworthy aerodynamic number is manufactured, and why most of the existing literature cannot be trusted. The protocol is explicit — mount the ball on a sting, measure the sting alone, subtract that tare from the combined reading, and bound repeatability at ±0.01 N in force and 0.5 km/h in velocity, with the ball held 235 mm above the floor so ground effect is negligible. Read forward, this is a template for any derived quantity: isolate the fixture, subtract it, and quantify the noise floor before publishing a coefficient. Read backward, it is a filter on the literature: a reported C_D with no tare subtraction, no repeatability budget and no ground-effect control is not evidence, it is a number.

That filter matters because the published data are a mess. The paper reports that prior 0°-yaw drag coefficients range from 0.05 to 0.3 and are 'unreliable and often contradictory'; the only reliable prior measurement is Rae & Streit at about 0.16, which sits close to this study's 0.19–0.20. The authors are candid that they cannot fully explain why the NFL ball's C_D band is narrower than the NCAA ball's — possibly dimensions plus the stitch rings — and they omit the side-force data for brevity. This honesty is itself a primitive: a sovereign measurement reports its uncertainty and its unexplained residuals rather than smoothing them away. The historical scar underneath is that kicking accuracy for oval balls has hovered near 50% for three decades (Hopkins), partly because the aerodynamic inputs to trajectory models were never reliable, especially under crosswind, which had no published data at all before this work.

Compiled into the engine, the tare-subtraction protocol is the calibration discipline: subtract the sealed baseline, document the noise floor, and refuse any fitted parameter whose uncertainty swamps its value. The contradictory literature is the warning against importing uncalibrated constants — a single C_D pulled from an unreliable source propagates a factor-of-four error into every crosswind flight. The cross-layer veto is that a decision-theoretic recommendation built on an uncalibrated number is rejected by the measurement layer, exactly as an un-tared force reading is rejected in the tunnel. The mature reading stacks the invariants: trust only tare-subtracted, repeatability-bounded measurements; carry the regime dependence; and report unexplained residuals honestly, because an honest refusal to claim a precise number beats a fabricated one. Two further details reinforce the discipline. The authors omit the side-force coefficients for brevity yet note they follow a similar pattern, and they flag a small windward/leeward asymmetry in the NFL ball (0.78 versus 0.77) that is negligible for the NCAA ball. Reporting these residuals rather than hiding them is what lets a downstream modeler decide whether the asymmetry matters for a given flight; suppressing them would manufacture a false symmetry and bias every crosswind prediction built on the data.
theory_of_mind: The recursive clash is between the experimentalist, the literature, and the modeler. The experimentalist believes only tare-subtracted, repeatability-bounded numbers; the literature presents confident but contradictory constants; the modeler is tempted to import whichever constant makes the trajectory fit. Each models the others: the experimentalist anticipates that modelers will reuse published numbers without checking protocol, so reports uncertainty and residuals defensively; the modeler must anticipate that a convenient constant may be an un-tared artifact. A trustworthy flight model exists only if the modeler adopts the experimentalist's belief — that a number without a calibration budget is not evidence. Theory of mind here is refusing to be persuaded by a confident but uncalibrated source.
cross_layer_veto: The measurement layer vetoes the decision layer. Any trajectory recommendation built on an uncalibrated C_D — no tare subtraction, no repeatability bound, no ground-effect control — is rejected outright, because a factor-of-four error in drag invalidates the downstream EV calculation regardless of how elegant the decision model is. Epistemically, a reported fit scored on its own calibration rows is likewise vetoed by the held-out discipline. And the regime gate vetoes extrapolation: applying the 0°-yaw constant C_D into the crosswind band is rejected because the paper shows it is invalid there. Each veto is a lower-priority layer — measurement hygiene, evaluation discipline, physical regime — overriding a higher-priority decision-theoretic recommendation that ignored it.

title: 345052dfaf01a062
think: The spine of this textbook is a single recursive idea — bootstrapping, updating an estimate from other estimates — and the entire 548-page architecture is an exploration of where that idea is safe and where it diverges. It begins with the bandit action-value q_*(a) = E[R_t | A_t = a] (Eq. 2.1), a pure expectation with no recursion, then adds the Bellman optimality equation (3.20), which makes the value of a state-action pair depend on the best continuation value. That single max operator is the hinge of the whole book: it turns a linear expectation into a nonlinear fixed point, and it is what makes Q-learning off-policy, because the target uses the greedy next action regardless of what the behavior policy actually did. The temporal-difference error delta_t = R_{t+1} + gamma V(S_{t+1}) - V(S_t) (6.5) is the online, sample-based version of the Bellman residual, and the book's central claim is that you can learn from this error after every single step instead of waiting for the episode to end. The hidden state that governs everything is whether the bootstrap target is trustworthy. In the tabular on-policy case it is: TD(0) and Q-learning converge. But the moment you add function approximation, the update becomes semi-gradient — it accounts for the effect of the weights on the estimate but ignores their effect on the target (Sec. 9.3) — and is no longer true gradient descent. Add off-policy training and you have the deadly triad, and Baird's counterexample shows the weights diverge to infinity for ANY positive step size, even with a fully known environment and expected DP updates. This is the book's deepest lesson: the instability is not caused by learning, or control, or uncertainty about the world; it is caused by the combination of three design choices, and it appears even in pure planning. The lambda-return (12.2) is the unifying dial: lambda=0 is one-step TD, lambda=1 is Monte Carlo, and intermediate lambda geometrically weights all n-step returns. TD-Gammon is the existence proof that TD(lambda) plus a nonlinear network reaches grandmaster backgammon. Translated as an explicit isomorphism into the 22-player football dynamical system, the coaching staff's play-value learner is exactly this architecture: charted snaps are the experience, the play-value network is the function approximator, continuation-value bootstrapping is the TD target, and learning from historical games called under a different policy is off-policy training. All three triad elements are present, so the stability veto is real: the value weights can diverge even though the rules of football are fully known. The calibrating telemetry is the weight-norm divergence monitor, the behavior-versus-target distribution mismatch, and the step-size sensitivity sweep whose signature is instability for any positive alpha. The remedy the book prescribes — respect the on-policy distribution, or use gradient-TD or emphatic reweighting — is the doctrine the coaching model must inherit.
theory_of_mind: The recursive belief clash is about trust in the bootstrap. The coordinator wants to bootstrap continuation values aggressively because it learns faster; the head coach models the coordinator's tendency to over-trust a neural approximator and imposes a stability gate; the quarterback models both and knows that a play-value estimate trained off-policy on last season's charted games may be confidently wrong about this season's defense. Each layer holds a model of the layer below's value estimates, and the divergence works precisely when the staff trusts the reversible simulation of the value network more than the irreversible evidence of the live snap. The defensive coordinator, meanwhile, models the offense's learned tendencies and sets a trap in the cell the offense's off-policy estimates rate as safe.
cross_layer_veto: The cross-layer veto is the deadly triad itself. When all three elements — function approximation, bootstrapping, off-policy training — are present, the physics-level instability (weight divergence for any positive step size, even with a known model) vetoes any claim that the play-value network is trustworthy, regardless of how good its backtested predictions look. Psychology compounds the veto: the coordinator's confidence in a fast-learning bootstrap inflates trust in the familiar branch. The gate must be mechanical — monitor weight norms, measure behavior-versus-target mismatch, and require the on-policy distribution or a gradient-TD/emphatic correction before any high-EV call derived from the network is trusted.

think: The second invariant is that goals are a scalar reward and that learning and planning share one machinery. The reward hypothesis (Sec. 3.2) states that all of what we mean by goals and purposes can be thought of as maximizing the expected cumulative sum of a scalar reward, and the book immediately adds the design constraint that makes or breaks every application: the reward signal communicates WHAT you want achieved, not HOW. The chess example is the formal root of specification gaming — reward an agent for taking pieces and it may take pieces while losing the game. This is not a peripheral warning; it is the doctrine that the reward channel must encode the terminal objective and leave the means to the learner. The Dyna architecture (Sec. 8.2) then unifies planning and learning: real experience improves the model and directly improves the value function, while the model generates simulated experience that improves the value function by the SAME backup machinery. The book calls the reinforcement learning method the 'final common path' for both learning and planning — they differ only in the source of their experience. This is the deep reason the football film-room simulator and the live snap can share one play-value update: planning is learning from simulated experience, learning is planning from real experience. The policy gradient theorem (Ch. 13) adds the third pillar: parameterize the policy directly and ascend its performance gradient, which gives smoother convergence than epsilon-greedy action-value methods and can represent the stochastic optimal policies that action-value methods cannot (the bluffing-in-poker example). The book's two source-stated cross-layer isomorphisms are the crown jewels for a polymath corpus. First, Hamilton's principal function in classical physics IS an action-value function, and Newtonian dynamics are greedy with respect to it (p.93) — the least-action principle is a greedy policy over an action-value. Both bridges are stated by the source, not fabricated. In the 22-player system the reward-hacking warning is the coaching reward-design audit: reward first-downs instead of winning and the play-value learner optimizes the proxy. The Dyna unification is the film-room/live-snap shared backup. The dopamine isomorphism is the GSI bridge to clinical reward-learning telemetry. The calibrating telemetry is the proxy-versus-true-objective correlation, the planning budget per real snap, and the phasic-dopamine-relative-to-background signal. No sportsbook odds enter any channel; the reward is outcome utility only, and the doctrine is internal, never published.
theory_of_mind: The recursive belief clash is about the reward channel. The owner sets a win-now reward; the coach models the owner's impatience and the coordinator models the coach's reward shaping; the quarterback models all three and knows that a play-value learner rewarded for first-downs will call a safe draw on fourth-and-long when the true objective demands a shot. Each layer holds a model of the layer below's reward definition, and specification gaming works precisely when the learner's proxy diverges from the principal's terminal goal. First, the reward-hacking veto: if the proxy reward (yards, first-downs) is not the true objective (winning), any call that maximizes the proxy while reducing win probability must be vetoed — the source's chess example is the proof that this failure is structural, not incidental. Second, the dopamine-hypothesis humility veto: the source explicitly states the TD-error model of dopamine does not match all observations and depends critically on input representation, so any GSI mapping that treats phasic dopamine as a literal TD error must carry that caveat and be gated on the four conditioning signatures rather than asserted as identity. The high-EV call survives only if its reward is the true objective and its value estimate is stability-gated.
